## Human-accepted Full V1 contract

This document is the single current authority for SCNSim V1 runtime semantics.
The complete dev1–dev6 scope is Human-`ACCEPTED`: primitive and Composite
authoring, Direct/root/CMA execution, RLGC and N-port selected networks,
PTC/transform/retain, typed Direct quantities, workspace evidence, and the
case-oriented JosephsonCircuits HB path taught through Lesson 13.

The complete dev1–dev6 Full V1 runtime scope is `STABILIZED`: its accepted
documentation, implementation, durable cross-slice tests, and validation
agree. This lifecycle state does not imply a release, main promotion, root
pin, or consumer migration.

The separate adaptive presentation-theme scope is a `CONVERGING` candidate.
It changes only how already-materialized diagrams, figures, and reports choose
colors; it does not reopen Full V1 numerical, workspace, or identity semantics.

For a Plan containing an `AffineMap`, dev5 applies the declared authorization
and records each authorized out-of-support consumer as extrapolation evidence.
:::

## Contract scope

After reading this contract, a package consumer should understand:

1. how the component-authoring contract produces the one physical Plan;
2. how one Plan produces several lazy reduction references;
3. which calls execute work and which calls only resolve sealed evidence;
4. how every physical value carries a checked unit;
5. which topology, coordinate, and boundary operations SCNSim applies to one
   declared circuit;
6. how Direct matrix responses and typed physical quantities share one
   evaluation contract;
7. how one HB request represents DC, AC, multi-tone, and mixed operating
   cases; and
8. which identities and artifacts make a result reproducible across Python
   processes.

This document defines public product/runtime behavior. Circuit physics,
scientific Gates, and consumer Design Targets remain in their own authorized
sources.

The linear [Tutorial](index.qmd) teaches these objects in first-use order. The
Concept pages explain the design pressures behind
[network views](concepts/compilation-coordinates-and-network-views.qmd),
[execution and Result ownership](concepts/requests-execution-and-result-ownership.qmd),
[Direct/HB realization](concepts/direct-and-hb-realizations.qmd), and
[optimization](concepts/units-parameters-and-optimization.qmd). This Contract
remains the exact authority for signatures, formulas, invariants, failures,
receipt evidence, and limits. The separate
[Implementation Design](contracts/index.qmd#implementation-design) explains how
the Runtime realizes this public behavior without becoming a second public
contract.

## Product and lifecycle boundary

SCNSim owns:

- Python circuit authoring and runtime interfaces;
- reusable component and visual catalogs;
- physical node-flux compilation and Direct C/K/G;
- coordinate transforms and Schur-complement reduction;
- Direct and harmonic-balance analysis;
- Direct optimization, immutable receipts, results, and reports; and
- authoring and compiler-expanded schematic projections of the original
  circuit plan.

SCNSim does not own:

- consumer Design Targets, optimization Gates, or consumer application
  notebook source;
- D3/IPF/NCUAS values, layouts, manifests, artifacts, or evidence;
- SCGSim layout/EM execution or OrPen PDK source;
- JosephsonCircuits as a library;
- quantization; or
- the legacy Circuit Workbench application and repository.

JosephsonCircuits is an HB backend. It is not the authority for SCNSim
topology, coordinate names, Direct operators, reductions, or public consumer
contracts.

SCNSim has no previously accepted or delivered Unit or Runtime API to migrate.
This document records the Human-accepted Full V1 contract in place. It does not
supersede, mutate, redirect, or provide compatibility for the legacy
Workbench. Reusable implementation may later be transplanted only from the
exact public handoff with its Git provenance.

## Runtime ownership model {#runtime-ownership-model}

### Four responsibilities

| Object | Owns | Does not own |
|---|---|---|
| `CircuitPlan` | Components, parameters, electric nodes, canonical ground, logical Ports, and catalog identities | Execution state or results |
| `NetworkViewRef` | One immutable Plan reference and ordered topology/view lineage | Compilation, workspace writes, or results |
| `CircuitRun` | One sealed Plan, workspace, runtime identity, requests, receipts, and execution | Circuit physics or a mutable current model/result |
| typed `AnalysisResult` | One verified request result and its exact evidence identity | Authority to mutate the Plan, Ref, or Run |

### Two users, one reusable model

The public SCNSim vocabulary serves two different layers:

| Layer | Primary objects | Repeated work it should avoid |
|---|---|---|
| Circuit-model development | `Library`, `CircuitPlan`, `NetworkViewRef`, quantity and solve Specs | Re-deriving physical topology or analysis semantics in every Notebook |
| Model consumption | A project-owned Design Target and thin Python façade returning typed Results | Restating components, electric nodes, ground attachments, logical Ports, objective selectors, weights, and optimizer controls |

The façade is ordinary consumer-package code, not a second SCNSim registry or
physical authority. It reconstructs the exact Plan/Ref/Spec request, so a
kernel-restarted consumer can call the same façade to `resolve()` exact durable
evidence. The model developer may expose `optimize_readout(target, workspace)`
or another domain-named function; SCNSim does not prescribe those project
names and does not own their Design Target.

The native-API micro-course keeps those responsibilities visible instead of
wrapping them in a project façade. Begin by
[authoring a primitive Plan](../examples/tutorials/01_author_primitive.qmd),
[optimizing its public parameter](../examples/tutorials/04_optimize_primitive.qmd),
then [creating a custom Library](../examples/tutorials/06_create_library.qmd),
[adding a Composite factory](../examples/tutorials/07_add_composite_factory.qmd),
and [using](../examples/tutorials/08_use_custom_component.qmd) its component. The
advanced lessons apply the same Run/Ref/Spec vocabulary directly to
[RLGC](../examples/tutorials/09_model_n_trace_line.qmd),
[PTC and transforms](../examples/tutorials/11_transform_retain.qmd), and
[Direct/HB comparison](../examples/tutorials/13_compare_direct_hb.qmd).

This separation is a UX boundary, not a second Runtime. Both users ultimately
receive the same typed SCNSim Results and exact receipt identities.

`CircuitPlan` is the only physical circuit authority. There is no
`ReducedCircuitPlan`; a Schur-complement model is an analysis reference derived
from the Plan, not a second circuit.

### Component authoring supplies the Plan

The [V1 Component Authoring contract](component-authoring.qmd) is the single
product authority for immutable built-in/custom Libraries, component factories,
pins, public/anonymous electric nodes, the automatic canonical ground, logical
Ports, and inductive coupling. The shortest authoring route is:

```python
from scnsim import CircuitPlan, components, units as u

plan = CircuitPlan(id="example")
readout_cap = plan.add(
    components.capacitor(
        id="readout_cap",
        capacitance=92.0 * u.fF,
    )
)
```

Every Plan owns the reserved `"ground"` identity from construction. Direct
uses it as the node-flux reference and HB lowers it to JosephsonCircuits node
`"0"`; the backend name is not a public coordinate. Generic components expose
`terminal_1`/`terminal_2`, while grounded resonators expose one non-reference
`terminal` and bind their internal return to that ground. Model authors use
repeatable `plan.ground(*pins)` calls only for ordinary pins that must join it.

Every public physical value uses the one `scnsim.units` Pint registry. Public
physical inputs do not accept bare numbers; a physically meaningful
dimensionless value uses `u.dimensionless`. Counts, indices, seeds, booleans,
enum choices, and other non-physical controls remain ordinary Python values.

The Runtime consumes the authored Plan. It does not maintain a mutable Library,
invent child-component parameters, or infer topology or units from a component
name.

### Seal one Plan into one Run

`CircuitRun` seals the Plan and binds it to one evidence workspace:

```python
from scnsim import CircuitRun

run = CircuitRun(
    plan=plan,
    workspace="results/example_run",
    versioned=False,
)

original = run.original
```

The Run has no global `action`, current Ref, current parameters, or current
result. `versioned=False` is the default topology-iteration policy: opening the
same workspace with a different successfully sealed Plan atomically replaces
the prior Plan workspace and its request evidence without a confirmation
prompt. Opening it with the same Plan identity reuses the existing workspace.

`versioned=True` preserves topologies beneath the selected parent workspace as
`iteration01`, `iteration02`, and so on. Each iteration is a complete ordinary
Plan workspace; the parent index maps Plan identity to iteration, and the same
Plan reuses its existing directory. Changing a Spec or ParameterSet alone does
not allocate an iteration.

An existing unversioned workspace may be upgraded atomically to
`versioned=True`; its current Plan becomes `iteration01` without changing its
requests. The reverse transition is forbidden before mutation because it would
delete evidence the user explicitly chose to preserve. The error directs the
user to supply a different workspace path for replacement mode.

Sealing is permanent for both that Run and the supplied Python Plan. The same
`CircuitRun` may execute any number of immutable Refs, Specs, and ParameterSets
derived from its sealed Plan; none
of those questions changes the Plan or invalidates earlier Results. Editing
sealed Plan content—including topology, an authoring baseline, Ports,
couplings, or a public component schema—raises `PlanSealedError`. The author
reruns the builder to create a new `CircuitPlan` and `CircuitRun`; the same
Python variable names and workspace path may be rebound without restarting the
kernel. Supplying a declared `ParameterSet` does not change topology.

In replacement mode, an older Run or lazy Result fails with
`WorkspacePlanReplacedError` once another Plan has replaced its backing
workspace. The check binds an evidence-only workspace-instance ID in addition
to the Plan hash, so an `A → B → A` sequence cannot accidentally revive the old
A handle. With `versioned=True`, each Run remains bound to its retained
iteration and may coexist with newer topology Runs.

### Declare the floating-qubit Ref graph without executing {#floating-qubit-ref-graph}

`run.original` is the zero-reduction root `NetworkViewRef`. `reduce()` returns
a new immutable Ref and never compiles, launches Julia, solves, or writes a
receipt:

```python
compensated = original.reduce(
    ReductionPipeline().ptc(
        probe_plus,
        probe_minus,
    )
)

qubit_modes = compensated.reduce(
    ReductionPipeline().transform_pair(
        "qubit_plus",
        "qubit_minus",
        id="qubit",
    )
)

qubit_differential = qubit_modes.reduce(
    ReductionPipeline().retain(
        "qubit.differential",
    )
)

feedline = qubit_modes.reduce(
    ReductionPipeline().retain(
        "feedline_in",
        "feedline_out",
    )
)

monitoring = qubit_modes.reduce(
    ReductionPipeline().retain(
        "feedline_in",
        "feedline_out",
        "monitor",
    )
)
```

Here `probe_plus` and `probe_minus` are the `PortRef` handles returned when the
Plan added the two logical probe Ports. `ptc()` removes their selected,
evidenced load stamps from the effective analysis topology.
`transform_pair()` replaces the ordered Public node pair with the generated
`qubit.common` and `qubit.differential` coordinates. `retain()` selects an
ordered, non-empty set of Public or generated node coordinates and
Schur-eliminates the complete complement under `I_external = 0`. None of these
declarations executes work.

The reusable point is the Ref itself:
`original -> compensated -> qubit_modes -> feedline`. A Ref may produce any
number of child Refs, so the same transformed ancestor can support a one-port
differential view, a two-port feedline view, and a larger monitoring view.
Pipeline step labels are evidence labels, not a second API such as
`model.at("checkpoint")`.

## Run operations and durable results

### One execution owner {#solve-versus-evaluate}

The Run performs every terminal operation, but `solve()` and `evaluate()` have
different user-visible jobs:

| Question | Call | Compatible Spec family | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| What is the selected-view S/Y/Z response over a grid? | `run.solve(ref, spec)` | `DirectSolveSpec` | Direct response matrices and named traces |
| What are the named HB case responses? | `run.solve(ref, spec)` | `HBSolveSpec` | `HBBatchResult` with one typed outcome per declared case |
| What is one Direct root, pole, zero, coupling, or response scalar? | `run.evaluate(ref, spec)` | Typed Direct quantity Spec | Typed quantity Result |
| What is the complete Direct dynamic operator? | `run.evaluate(ref, spec)` | `OperatorSpec` | `OperatorResult` |
| Which parameters minimize declared typed quantity objectives? | `run.optimize(ref, spec)` | `OptimizationSpec` | `OptimizationResult` |

The `SolveSpec` suffix means “produce a response surface.” A
`DirectSolveSpec` solves the complete selected-view N-port response over its
declared grid. It does not guess S21: a one-port view yields S11, a two-port
view yields the complete 2-by-2 response, and an N-port view yields the
complete N-by-N response. Named `SParameterTrace` objects are typed projections
of that same result and never launch another solve.
`SolveSpec` is only the category name used by this contract; V1 does not add an
abstract public `SolveSpec` class. Consumers construct `DirectSolveSpec` or
`HBSolveSpec` directly.

The stabilized Full V1 runtime supports `DirectSolveSpec` on every final View that proves
its ordered terminal basis is Port-realizable. It publishes the complete
finite N-port S/Y/Z matrices once, then projects any declared named traces from
that same result. A non-realizable final View fails closed rather than
returning an incomplete or fabricated wave response.

A Direct quantity Spec instead asks `evaluate()` for one defined physical
quantity without creating an unrelated response sweep. `DiagonalRootSpec`, for
example, runs the required-hint deterministic Newton procedure on one physically
anchored coordinate's operator diagonal and returns its machine-resolved root,
frequency, linewidth, and local slope evidence. The coordinate owns physical
identity; `root_hint` only initializes the baseline Newton basin.
`ResponseElementSpec` may
evaluate one explicitly selected S/Y/Z scalar at one frequency, but it still
does not imply a frequency-grid response. `OperatorSpec` is the deliberate
exception that materializes the complete labeled Direct operator.

These combinations fail closed before execution:

```python
run.solve(feedline, DiagonalRootSpec(...))
run.evaluate(feedline, DirectSolveSpec(...))
```

The valid operations remain independent exact requests:

```python
direct = run.solve(feedline, DirectSolveSpec(...))
hb = run.solve(feedline, HBSolveSpec(...))
readout = run.evaluate(feedline, DiagonalRootSpec(...))
optimization = run.optimize(feedline, OptimizationSpec(...))
```

`solve()`, `evaluate()`, and `optimize()` are real actions. They compute the
exact request identity, materialize missing dependencies in order, write
sealed request/receipt/artifact evidence, and return the corresponding typed
Result. They do not mutate the Plan or Ref and do not save a result as mutable
state on the Run.

Presentation is never another action:

```python
from scnsim import Theme

direct.s.show(magnitude="db", theme=Theme.AUTO)
direct.traces["transmission"].show(magnitude="db", theme=Theme.DARK)
readout.show()
```

These calls read the typed Results already returned above. They do not solve,
recompute, interpolate, or select a latest request.

### Use response and quantity Results together

One Notebook may legitimately need both the response surface and a physical
quantity. It declares two Specs and executes two explicit requests against the
same sealed Run and Ref:

```python
reflection_trace = SParameterTrace(
    id="reflection",
    input_port="signal_in",
    input_mode=(),
    output_port="signal_in",
    output_mode=(),
)
direct_spec = DirectSolveSpec(
    frequencies=frequency_grid,
    traces=(reflection_trace,),
)
root_spec = DiagonalRootSpec(
    coordinate="readout_node",
    root_hint=6.0 * u.GHz,
)

direct = run.solve(view, direct_spec)
root = run.evaluate(view, root_spec)

report = run.build_report(
    ReportSpec(inputs=(direct, root), theme=Theme.AUTO)
)
```

The two requests may reuse exact sealed compile/dependency evidence, but there
is no hidden current Result and neither request changes the meaning of the
other. The Report records both exact input identities rather than deriving the
root from a plotted S minimum or pretending the diagonal root is S21.

### Request identity and immutable attempts {#request-identity-and-immutable-attempts}

A canonical request identifies the sealed Plan, Ref, Spec, ParameterSet,
runtime, and operation. Execution history is not part of that identity. If the
request already has one complete verified success receipt, the operation
reuses that Result without recomputing or overwriting it.

The workspace path is an evidence location, not part of computational request
identity. A leaf workspace binds one Plan; each request binds its semantic
runtime. `CircuitRun` resolves the request only inside that Plan workspace. A
different or relocated workspace does not rename the request, but it may not
contain the required receipt.

If every prior attempt failed or was interrupted, calling the same operation
again keeps the canonical request identity and appends a new immutable attempt.
Earlier requests, logs, failure receipts, and partial artifacts remain
auditable; there is no force-overwrite flag and no mutable current attempt.
Only the operation methods create attempts. `resolve()` never retries, resumes,
or launches work.

Attempt ordinals start at one and use a minimum width of six decimal digits:
`attempts/000001/`, `attempts/000002/`, and so on. Values beyond six digits
grow naturally without an artificial maximum. Before promotion, the same
ordinal appears in
`attempts/.staging-000001-<lowercase-canonical-UUIDv4>/`. An ordinal spelling,
UUID form, final directory, or staging directory that does not match its
sealed attempt evidence fails integrity validation; path formatting is not an
implementation choice.

### Explain before execution

V1 does not expose a public JobRef layer. A consumer can inspect a request
without executing it:

```python
run.explain(feedline, direct_spec).show()
```

`explain()` performs the same deterministic ParameterSet binding and compile
preflight needed to resolve topology and coordinate evidence, but it does not
launch a solver, create a request directory, or write the workspace. The
explanation identifies the sealed Plan, selected Ref, effective parameters,
operation/backend, grids, reduction lineage, runtime, and exact dependency
graph. It expands every component to its backend rows, shows Library/schema
identity, component-pin to electric-node/ground mapping, Public/Internal/
Port-promoted node identities, explicit local ground groups, logical Port
attachments and namespace mapping,
Direct `B`/`Y0`/load/wave lowering, HB `P`/`R_port` lowering,
SQUID loop orientation, and every bound inductive-coupling `L1`, `L2`, signed
`k`, derived `M`, and backend map. For an automatic paired-node transform it
also shows every included
external-cut capacitance branch, every excluded direct-mutual branch, the
resolved weights and transform, the transformed reference matrix and principal
root, Port-realizability, and the ordered mode-port realization. It also lists
the retained/eliminated coordinates, final selected-view channel order,
induced `A_k`/`B_k`/`R_k`/`D_k`, and per-probe raw/compensated load state. HB
explanations additionally show the exact source-coefficient index/conjugation
map, signed nonzero response frequencies, and input/output `W` conversion for
solver-native Z and S.
Optimization explanations show
each required root hint and baseline branch selection, the expanded relative or
explicit residual scales, quantity dependency graph, shared
compile/factorization/root work, Julia execution boundary, and baseline
resolution; candidate-specific continuations remain in candidate receipts.

### Resolve without execution

`resolve()` accepts the same Ref, spec, and optional ParameterSet as the
corresponding operation. Because `optimize(ref, spec)` always starts from the
sealed Plan baseline, its matching `resolve(ref, optimization_spec)` and
`explain(ref, optimization_spec)` forms do not accept an external
`ParameterSet`:

```python
direct = run.resolve(feedline, direct_spec)
```

It recomputes the expected request identity, then reads and verifies the sealed
workspace request, receipt, and artifacts. It never executes, searches for a
latest stage, retries a failed or interrupted attempt, or relies on a
process-local cache. The same call must therefore work after a Notebook kernel
restart when every bound identity remains exact. Missing, stale, corrupt, or
mismatched evidence fails closed with the missing or mismatched identity named.

`run.inventory()` is a shared-lock, read-only inspection of the exact leaf
bound to that `CircuitRun`. A replaceable workspace lists only its active leaf;
a versioned Run lists only its own iteration, never sibling iterations. A
stale Run raises `WorkspacePlanReplacedError`. Requests are ordered by
`request_sha256`, attempt ordinals are numeric ascending, and request status is
`succeeded` when a verified success exists or otherwise the failure/interruption
state of the greatest finalized ordinal. A verified HB batch remains
`succeeded` even when every case is a numerical failure. Hidden staging is not
an attempt; an empty request, broken hash chain, or invalid finalized attempt
is `EvidenceIntegrityError` rather than an omitted row. Inventory never writes
evidence and does not establish a hidden current/latest selection for
`resolve()`, reports, or any other API.

## Units, identity, and parameter variants

### Canonical SI identity

At every Python trust boundary, SCNSim validates Quantity dimensionality and
normalizes physical values to coherent SI for compilation, hashing, and Julia
transport:

```text
SCNSim-registry Quantity
-> validate declared dimensionality
-> canonical SI magnitude + SI unit
-> compile/request identity
```

The sealed representation records:

- canonical SI magnitude and unit;
- physical dimensionality;
- preferred declaration/display unit; and
- original input magnitude and unit as provenance.

Receipts do not pickle Pint objects. They serialize magnitudes, units, and
dimensionality so another process can reconstruct a Quantity with the same
SCNSim registry. This follows Pint's guidance for a shared application
registry and durable serialization:

- [Using Pint in a project](https://pint.readthedocs.io/en/latest/getting/pint-in-your-projects.html)
- [Serializing Pint quantities](https://pint.readthedocs.io/en/stable/advanced/serialization.html)

Physically identical `92.0 * u.fF` and `0.092 * u.pF` produce the same
computational identity after canonicalization. Their source units remain
visible provenance and may be displayed differently without splitting the
physical request identity.
The receipt preserves the source spelling used by the executed attempt. A
later semantic-equivalent reuse returns that verified evidence and does not
append a new attempt merely to log the caller's alternate spelling.

### Static and runtime checks

Public type annotations require `pint.Quantity` with the appropriate magnitude
container, which lets static analysis reject an ordinary float passed to a
Quantity-only interface. Pint's generic annotation does not encode physical
dimensionality, so F-versus-H correctness is enforced at runtime by
`ParameterSpec`, Plan seal, `ParameterSet`, and operation-boundary validation.
SCNSim does not add a parallel phantom-type unit system. See
[Pint typing](https://pint.readthedocs.io/en/stable/advanced/typing.html).

### Explicit ParameterSet variants

The sealed Plan supplies the baseline parameters. An operation may instead
receive an immutable `ParameterSet` keyed by Plan-derived `ParameterRef`
objects:

```python
candidate = ParameterSet({
    readout_cap.parameter("capacitance"): 95.0 * u.fF,
})

candidate_direct = run.solve(
    feedline,
    direct_spec,
    parameters=candidate,
)
```

Omitting `parameters=` uses the sealed baseline. Supplying a ParameterSet does
not bind or mutate the Ref; the ParameterSet is part of that operation's exact
request identity. A ParameterSet with unknown refs, incompatible units,
non-finite values, or a different Plan family fails before execution.

Optimization exposes its selected parameters through the same type:

```python
optimization = run.optimize(feedline, optimization_spec)

winner_hb = run.solve(
    feedline,
    final_hb_spec,
    parameters=optimization.best.parameters,
)
```

The new HB request uses the explicitly selected `feedline` lineage plus the
winner ParameterSet. A ParameterSet never carries or changes a Ref lineage;
the optimization source remains parameter provenance.

## Shared topology and unified node views {#shared-topology-and-unified-node-views}

`ReductionPipeline` is one ordered, backend-neutral node-coordinate lineage.
It never chooses Direct or HB. A topology step changes the effective circuit
analyzed by descendants; a view step changes the coordinates or boundary used
to inspect that circuit. Both backends consume the same Ref and either realize
it faithfully or fail before solver execution.

### Selective Port-Termination Compensation (PTC) is a shared topology step

The `ptc()` step explicitly receives one or more `nonloading_probe` `PortRef`
handles from the same Plan:

```python
compensated = run.original.reduce(
    ReductionPipeline().ptc(
        probe_plus,
        probe_minus,
    )
)
```

For every selected Port, the sealed compiled artifact must prove one exact
node attachment, finite positive reference impedance, load stamp, and
backend-lowering identity. The explicit `ptc()` call supplies removal intent;
the Port role or a caller-provided resistance alone does not. Physical and
environmental loads that are not selected remain in the effective circuit.

A lineage may contain PTC at most once. It must precede `transform_pair()` and
`retain()`, and every descendant Ref inherits the same compensation set.
`retain()` is the terminal basis selection for that lineage. Unknown, repeated,
terminated, foreign, or unevidenced targets fail before execution.

For Direct analysis, the source-loaded operator first supports the raw solve;
the selected-network adapter then de-embeds all source resistors and re-adds
only the omitted, non-PTC matched loads according to the common load mask.
This is algebraically the explicit removal of each selected probe stamp, but it
does not confuse a selected source resistor with DUT admittance. SCNSim owns:

```text
C: capacitance
K: stiffness / inverse inductance
G: conductance
D(omega) = K - omega^2 C - i omega G
```

Direct optimization recompiles every candidate ParameterSet and replays the
complete PTC and view lineage. It never optimizes a nominal matrix that still
contains the artificial loss channel.

### Automatic paired-node coordinates are a shared view step

`transform_pair()` declares one ordered pair of distinct Public node
coordinates and one output namespace. Inputs may be Plan `ElectricNodeRef`
handles, composite `CoordinateRef` handles, or declared coordinate-ID strings:

```python
qubit_modes = compensated.reduce(
    ReductionPipeline().transform_pair(
        "qubit_plus",
        "qubit_minus",
        id="qubit",
    )
)
```

The two inputs are replaced by the ordered outputs `qubit.common` and
`qubit.differential`. The Ref stores the input pair, output namespace, and the
automatic rule; it never stores nominal numeric weights and V1 exposes no
manual-weight override through this operation.

The scientific definition is canonical in
[Admittance Coordinate Transforms](https://github.com/arfiligol/SCQ_Design/blob/main/docs/knowledge/network-modeling/admittance-coordinate-transforms.qmd#full-external-cut-weighting).
After binding the operation's complete ParameterSet, SCNSim enumerates the
original compiled reciprocal lumped capacitance branches. Each node's
external cut includes capacitance to ground/reference and to every node outside
the selected pair; every direct mutual branch between the selected nodes is
excluded from the weights but remains in the differential energy and compiled
operator.

This rule selects deterministic floating-pair coordinates. It does not claim
to diagonalize a loaded network, a frequency-dependent admittance, an already
Schur-reduced environment, a distributed model, or an operating-point
linearization. External coordinates may remain coupled to both generated
coordinates.

PTC and `transform_pair()` are independent declarations. A transform neither
requires nor inserts PTC and may act on ordinary Public nodes or nodes with
logical Port attachments. If a lineage contains both, the explicit PTC step
comes first so the topology change remains visible; PTC changes evidenced
conductance stamps and does not change capacitance-derived weights.

Direct operations apply the resolved power-conjugate transform to the selected
operator. HB repeats that same real transform independently inside every
retained sideband mode. Direct optimization resolves the external cut again
from every candidate's original compiled capacitance operator rather than
reusing baseline weights.

The selected-view S matrix uses the generalized real-SPD matrix-reference
power-wave contract from
[Port Reference Impedance Semantics](https://github.com/arfiligol/SCQ_Design/blob/main/docs/knowledge/simulation/port-reference-impedance-semantics.qmd#real-spd-matrix-reference-power-waves).
SCNSim transforms the declared physical reference matrix with the resolved
coordinate map and uses its principal symmetric SPD square root. It does not
replace a non-diagonal transformed reference with diagonal entries. Direct and
HB therefore expose the same selected-view wave convention even when the
backend-native HB convention differs.

### Retain an arbitrary node-coordinate view

`retain()` accepts any ordered, non-empty set of unique Public or generated
coordinates from the current basis. A selector is a Plan `ElectricNodeRef`, a
composite-exposed `CoordinateRef`, or a declared coordinate-ID string. Handles
are preferred while authoring one live Plan. Strings are required for
transform-generated coordinates and remain valid for named or Port-promoted
Public coordinates at serialized/team-facade boundaries:

```python
feedline = compensated.reduce(
    ReductionPipeline().retain(
        feedline_in_node,
        feedline_out_node,
    )
)

filter_quantities = compensated.reduce(
    ReductionPipeline().retain(
        ipf.coordinate("filter_open_tail"),
    )
)
```

The listed coordinates become the selected-view order. Every coordinate in the
complete complement is dynamically Schur-eliminated with zero external current
while loads already present in the effective operator remain. Anonymous
Internal nodes are never directly selectable and therefore remain in that
complement. `N=1` and `N=2` are ordinary one- and two-coordinate cases, not
separate APIs.

The selected-view wave-channel ID is exactly its final retained coordinate ID.
For an original node this is its Public node ID; for an automatic transform it
is the generated ID such as `qubit.differential`. A logical Port ID is not a
channel alias. Only anonymous-node promotion deliberately makes a node ID equal
to its Port ID. Unknown or foreign handles/IDs, generated-output collisions,
and duplicate retained identities fail before any trace is bound. A
`CoordinateRef` can be observed but cannot be passed to `CircuitPlan.net()` or
`add_port()`; the composite must expose a separate `PinRef` for external
wiring.

A probe-free feedline S21 therefore requires both operations:

1. `ptc()` removes the artificial probe shunt; and
2. `retain()` excludes that probe coordinate from the selected external set.

If a compensated probe remains in the retained set, a requested S matrix still
applies its declared matched-wave boundary. Energy coupled into that retained
external port is correct N-port scattering behavior, not a failed PTC.

Zero-current coordinate elimination is the boundary operation described by
[Schur Complement and Kron Reduction](https://github.com/arfiligol/SCQ_Design/blob/main/docs/knowledge/numerical-methods/schur-complement-kron-reduction.qmd#zero-current-schur-versus-matched-wave-submatrices).
It is not equivalent to selecting the same rows and columns from a native S
matrix, because omitted native incident waves leave those ports terminated in
their wave references.

### Terminal-operation capability

The pipeline vocabulary stays common while terminal operations enforce what
they can physically publish:

| Selected coordinate | Direct `evaluate()` / `optimize()` | Direct `solve()` | HB `solve()` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Public node without a logical Port | Yes | No | No |
| Public node with one logical Port | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Generated coordinate from an invertible transform of a complete Port-bound node subspace | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Generated coordinate involving a non-Port-bound node | Yes | No | No |
| Anonymous Internal node | Not directly selectable | Not directly selectable | Not directly selectable |

`solve()` always promises a complete selected-view S/Y/Z surface, so every
final coordinate must be port-realizable: either one original node with a
unique logical Port, or a generated coordinate from an invertible transform of
a complete Port-bound node subspace. Direct does not return a special
matrix-only solve result when this is false; it fails closed. Direct
`evaluate()` and `optimize()` may still inspect a named unported Public node in
the complete node operator because they do not promise a wave-port response.

When no explicit `retain()` exists, `solve()` uses all logical Ports in Plan
declaration order. `evaluate()` and Direct `optimize()` may instead work from
the full node operator and their named quantity selectors. HB may omit some
Port-bound nodes from the selected view: its full nonlinear/static balance
still includes every logical Port and load, then the linearized raw Z/Y
operator eliminates omitted channels with `I_external = 0`.

### One logical Port, two backend lowerings

A logical Port is a specialized `CircuitPlan` component, not a Library factory
and not a JosephsonCircuits row exposed as the product API:

| Port content | Direct | HB / JosephsonCircuits |
|---|---|---|
| Node attachment | incidence/selector column `B` | resolved node of `P_i` and `R_port_i` |
| Reference impedance | `Y0 = 1 / R0` and power-wave conversion | explicit `R_port_i` and solver port impedance |
| Port marker | no `P` row | exact `P_i` row |
| Source/load boundary | `G_port = B Y0 B^T` during raw solve | explicit source resistor stamp |
| Drive | external current injection through `B` | mode-indexed current on `P_i` |
| PTC | clear proved probe entry in the post-de-embedding load mask | clear the same proved probe entry in every sideband load mask |

The load and wave reference are separately auditable. PTC removes only the
load stamp; it preserves the logical Port identity, node coordinate, and
reference impedance required to define the selected S surface. Direct never
creates a fake `P` element merely to resemble the HB backend. Its receipt says
`P row = not applicable` and records the actual selector, reference-admittance,
voltage/current, load, and wave-conversion mapping. HB records the exact `P_i`
and `R_port_i` rows, solver indices, modes, and port order.

For both lowerings, Port voltage is the attached-node voltage relative to the
Plan ground and positive Port current enters the Plan at that node. The
canonical node attachment therefore owns direction; there is no backend- or
request-specific orientation override.

The logical Port resistance is a wave/source boundary, not a DUT shunt in the
public network. It participates in the raw solve and therefore supplies the
external damping of the solved problem, but SCNSim de-embeds the selected
source boundary before publishing `.y.view`, `.z.view`, and `.s.view`.

Let `B_p` inject the ordered original logical-Port currents into the full node
basis and let

$$
R_p=\operatorname{diag}(R_1,\ldots,R_P),
\qquad D_p=R_p^{1/2}.
$$

After backend normalization, SCNSim first removes *all* backend `P + R` source
resistors to recover the intrinsic linearized circuit operator. PTC then
defines a diagonal original-Port load mask `M`: `M[i,i] = 0` only for an
explicitly selected `nonloading_probe`; every other logical Port load remains
active. This mask is independent of whether a Port is retained or omitted.

For a Port-realizable selected view, let $A_k$ map ordered original-Port
voltages to the final retained voltages. Power-conjugate injection and the
matrix reference are

$$
B_k=B_pA_k^T,
\qquad R_k=A_kR_pA_k^T,
\qquad D_k=R_k^{1/2}.
$$

`D_k` is the principal real-SPD square root. Define the power-wave row map and
its selected/omitted projectors in original Port space:

$$
Q_k=D_k^{-1}A_kD_p,
\qquad P_k=Q_k^TQ_k,
\qquad P_o=I-P_k.
$$

These wave-boundary objects exist only when the terminal View is
Port-realizable. Retaining an unported Public node does not turn that node into
a Port and does not define $A_k$, $B_k$, $R_k$, $D_k$, $Q_k$, $P_k$, $P_o$, or
an omitted matched-load matrix. Its lineage stores the canonical not-applicable
representation for every such field: an `evidenceMatrix` with `rows=0` and
`columns=0`, whose SHA-256 covers the closed
`applicability=not_port_realizable` envelope. The source-boundary and
de-embedding hashes cover matching closed not-applicable envelopes. This is an
identity sentinel, not a zero-valued physical Port model.

The retained node and its complement remain exact node-coordinate lineage.
Direct quantity evaluation forms the complete loaded node operator—including
every logical-Port load not removed by PTC—and Schur-eliminates the complement
under zero external current. It may therefore evaluate a loaded node root.
`solve()` fails capability preflight on the same View before execution because
no S/Y/Z wave network exists there.

V1 requires a transformed pair to have one common load state: both original
Port loads are selected by PTC or neither is. That restriction makes the
retained and load partitions separable. A mixed-state pair fails preflight
rather than silently assigning a fractional load to the generated channels.
The omitted matched-load conductance in original Port coordinates is

$$
G_{o,p}=D_p^{-1}P_oMP_oD_p^{-1}.
$$

Let $Y_{\mathrm{circ,node}}$ be the intrinsic, source-resistor-de-embedded
Direct or normalized HB linearized node admittance. SCNSim applies this exact
selected-network order:

1. add omitted matched loads,
   $H=Y_{\mathrm{circ,node}}+B_pG_{o,p}B_p^T$;
2. add only the selected source boundary and solve
   $$
   Z_{\mathrm{src},k}
   =B_k^T(H+B_kR_k^{-1}B_k^T)^{-1}B_k;
   $$
3. obtain $Y_{\mathrm{src},k}$ by a matrix solve and de-embed the selected
   source boundary,
   $$Y_{\mathrm{net},k}=Y_{\mathrm{src},k}-R_k^{-1};$$
4. form public $Z_{\mathrm{net},k}$ from that same network Y; and
5. form the matrix-reference power-wave response

$$
\widetilde Y_k=D_kY_{\mathrm{net},k}D_k,
\qquad
S^{\mathrm{view}}=(I+\widetilde Y_k)^{-1}(I-\widetilde Y_k).
$$

Every inverse symbol above defines an equation, not an implementation method;
factorizations and linear solves are required. A rank-deficient $A_k$,
non-SPD $R_k$, singular selected solve, or incompatible load partition fails
closed.

The three public families now describe one de-embedded network:

$$
Y^{\mathrm{view}}=Y_{\mathrm{net},k},\qquad
Z^{\mathrm{view}}=Z_{\mathrm{net},k},\qquad
S^{\mathrm{view}}=S(Y_{\mathrm{net},k},R_k).
$$

An open one-port therefore has `Y_net = 0` and `S11 = +1`; a DUT whose
intrinsic input admittance is `1 / R0` has `S11 = 0`. Omitted terminated Ports
remain matched environmental loads. PTC changes only the explicitly selected
probe entries of `M`; it never de-embeds an unrelated physical/environmental
load. The typed matrix view continues to record each relevant probe as `raw`
or `compensated`, but the selected source boundary is never mislabeled as DUT.

### HB PTC operator realization

JosephsonCircuits first solves each case on the original compiled Plan. SCNSim
requests the complete solver-native `mode × port` `returnZ` operator. Let
`Pi_in` and `Pi_out` reorder solver modes to the SCNSim ordering by the *same
signed physical frequency*. Returned Z uses both the solver's
`exp(+i * omega * t)` convention and its `1 / sqrt(abs(omega))` input/output
scaling, so SCNSim forms exactly

$$
Z_{\mathrm{phys}}^{(-)} =
W_{\mathrm{out}}
\left[
\Pi_{\mathrm{out}}Z_{\mathrm{JC}}^{(+)}\Pi_{\mathrm{in}}^T
\right]^*
W_{\mathrm{in}}^{-1}.
$$

SCNSim conjugates once and does not also reverse Fourier tuples. Only this
convention- and frequency-normalized physical Z may be used to recover the raw
source-loaded admittance by a matrix solve. The adapter then follows one
ordered path:

1. normalize complete HB `returnZ` as above;
2. de-embed all backend `P + R` source resistors, recovering the intrinsic
   linearized circuit operator;
3. resolve the original-Port PTC mask `M` and apply the same mask to every
   retained sideband replica;
4. repeat the full-external-cut transform in every retained sideband mode;
5. build `A_k`, `B_k`, `R_k`, `D_k`, `Q_k`, and the selected/omitted projectors;
6. add omitted matched loads;
7. add the selected source boundary and solve the source-loaded response;
8. subtract `R_k^-1` from the selected source admittance; and
9. form public Y, Z, and S from that one de-embedded selected network.

The solver's mode tuples, signed physical frequencies, frequency
normalization, port order, and version are part of this operator identity.
Native `returnS` is requested only when the observable or reconciliation
evidence needs it; it is not a second topology authority.

Native `returnS` uses the same solver convention and byte scaling. When it is
requested for observable or reconciliation evidence, SCNSim independently
forms

$$
S_{\mathrm{native,pw}}^{(-)} =
W_{\mathrm{out}}
\left[
\Pi_{\mathrm{out}}S_{\mathrm{JC}}^{(+)}\Pi_{\mathrm{in}}^T
\right]^*
W_{\mathrm{in}}^{-1}.
$$

Here each diagonal `W` entry is `sqrt(abs(omega))` for the corresponding
ordered input or output mode. This is the normalized backend-native evidence
documented under
[JosephsonCircuits photon-flux-to-power normalization](https://github.com/arfiligol/SCQ_Design/blob/main/docs/knowledge/simulation/port-reference-impedance-semantics.qmd#josephsoncircuits-photon-flux-to-power-normalization).
Signed frequencies, the solver-to-SCNSim mode map, phasor convention, and mode
order remain evidence; only each `W` factor uses absolute frequency magnitude.
Because JosephsonCircuits `returnZ` itself divides the response and source
coordinates by `sqrt(abs(omega))`, every input and output mode of the requested
linear-response operator must have nonzero signed physical frequency. A DC
component may remain in the nonlinear/static balance, but a zero-frequency
linear-response mode makes the complete HBSolveSpec fail preflight; SCNSim does
not publish only Y/Z or silently drop that mode.

### Named HB drives, cases, mixing, and driven PTC {#named-hb-drives-cases-and-mixing}

One `HBSolveSpec` owns an ordered frequency lattice, immutable drive channels,
truncation, and named cases. A drive declares where one Fourier current enters;
each case supplies that drive's current:

```python
pump_a = PumpAxis(id="pump_a", frequency=7.0 * u.GHz)
pump_b = PumpAxis(id="pump_b", frequency=7.3 * u.GHz)

dc_bias = CurrentDrive(id="dc_bias", at=flux_port, mode=(0, 0))
pump_a_drive = CurrentDrive(
    id="pump_a_drive", at=flux_port, mode=(1, 0)
)
pump_b_drive = CurrentDrive(
    id="pump_b_drive", at=flux_port, mode=(0, 1)
)

hb = run.solve(
    feedline,
    HBSolveSpec(
        pump_axes=(pump_a, pump_b),
        drives=(dc_bias, pump_a_drive, pump_b_drive),
        frequencies=signal_grid,
        traces=(
            SParameterTrace(
                id="signal_gain",
                input_port="feedline_in",
                input_mode=(0, 0),
                output_port="feedline_out",
                output_mode=(0, 0),
            ),
            SParameterTrace(
                id="idler_conversion",
                input_port="feedline_in",
                input_mode=(0, 0),
                output_port="feedline_out",
                output_mode=(1, -1),
            ),
        ),
        cases=(
            HBCaseSpec(id="unbiased", currents={}),
            HBCaseSpec(
                id="dc_only",
                currents={dc_bias: 120.0 * u.uA},
            ),
            HBCaseSpec(
                id="dc_pump_a_low",
                currents={
                    dc_bias: 120.0 * u.uA,
                    pump_a_drive: 0.4 * u.uA,
                },
            ),
            HBCaseSpec(
                id="dc_two_tone",
                currents={
                    dc_bias: 120.0 * u.uA,
                    pump_a_drive: 0.4 * u.uA,
                    pump_b_drive: 0.2j * u.uA,
                },
            ),
        ),
        truncation=HBTruncation(
            pump_harmonics=(3, 3),
            modulation_harmonics=(1, 1),
            max_intermodulation_order=3,
            three_wave_mixing=True,
            four_wave_mixing=True,
        ),
        allow_driven_ptc=True,
    ),
)
```

Here `flux_port` is the `PortRef` returned by `plan.add_port()`. A
`CurrentDrive` cannot target a node ID or selected-view channel string.
Conversely, each `SParameterTrace.input_port` and `output_port` names a
selected-view wave channel; after `transform_pair()` that channel need not map
to one original `PortRef`.

`PumpAxis` declares one independent strong-tone fundamental. A commensurate
higher tone is a higher integer mode on the same fundamental, not another
axis. `CurrentDrive` owns only its ID, physical location, oriented injection
map, and mode; it never owns a current. An omitted case binding materializes as
exact `0 * u.A`.

Case values are complex Fourier-series coefficients, not peak or RMS phasors:

$$
i(t)=\sum_{\mathbf m} I_{\mathbf m}
e^{-i\mathbf m\cdot\boldsymbol\omega_p t}.
$$

For a real current, `I[-m] = conj(I[m])`; therefore a single nonzero-mode
coefficient has physical sinusoidal peak amplitude `2 * abs(I[m])`. SCNSim
generates the negative-mode conjugate from each declared nonzero-mode drive and
rejects an independently declared conjugate partner. The all-zero DC
coefficient is self-conjugate and must be real. The sealed schema records this
coefficient convention, source phase/calibration provenance, and every
oriented injection map `B_l`.

Backend lowering translates the convention before solving. The coefficient
identity is

$$
I_{\mathbf n}^{(+)}=I_{-\mathbf n}^{(-)}.
$$

If JosephsonCircuits retains representative tuple `r`, SCNSim therefore writes

$$
I_{\mathrm{JC}}^{(+)}[r]=I_{\mathrm{SCN}}^{(-)}[-r].
$$

For a user-declared coefficient `c` at tuple `m`, the same numeric tuple
receives `conj(c)`; the opposite tuple receives `c`. The exact-zero DC
coefficient is real and unchanged. Port-orientation sign is applied separately
from this phasor/mode conversion. The adapter materializes the generated
conjugate pair and then performs one index lookup; it must not both reverse a
tuple and conjugate the same coefficient a second time. This map is part of
request/receipt identity, so a complex pump phase cannot pass through by
accident.

Sources superpose in the compiled source vector,

$$
\mathbf u_{\mathbf m}=\sum_\ell
\mathbf B_\ell I_{\ell,\mathbf m}.
$$

Only contributions with the same oriented injection map may be collapsed to a
scalar effective current; different locations or orientations remain distinct
vector contributions. Accumulation follows drive declaration order and
evidence retains every contribution, generated conjugate, injection map, and
effective source vector.

`pump_axes=()` and `mode=()` form the pure-DC case. Otherwise every drive and
trace tuple rank and order match `pump_axes`. All cases share this request-wide
basis, drive schema, truncation, and mixing selection; a different basis or
selection is a different `HBSolveSpec` and `HBBatchResult`.
If any declared drive uses the all-zero mode, DC terms are enabled for the
whole batch so every case remains comparable; a case may still bind that drive
to exact zero.

Classification happens after ParameterSet binding, Quantity validation,
conjugate generation, and orientation-aware source-vector accumulation:

- any nonzero effective all-zero-mode current makes `BiasState.ON`;
- any nonzero effective nonzero-mode current makes `PumpState.ON`; and
- a DC-only case is Bias-on and Pump-off.

Exact cancellation produces the corresponding Off state; SCNSim invents no
near-zero tolerance. Case IDs remain the only public lookup identity. They name
declared experimental conditions, not Bias/Pump classifications, and remain in
declaration order under `hb.cases[id]`.

Three-wave and four-wave mixing are request-global model selections, not pump
counts or separate runs. `HBTruncation.three_wave_mixing` and
`four_wave_mixing` are required booleans. When both are enabled, one combined
Fourier-lattice nonlinear balance and one combined linearized response retain
both interaction families. When both are disabled, the result is explicitly a
mixing-disabled comparison and cannot be labeled a nonlinear mixing result.
The reusable physics remains canonical under
[source superposition and generated mixing](https://github.com/arfiligol/SCQ_Design/blob/main/docs/knowledge/numerical-methods/harmonic-balance-periodic-steady-state.qmd#source-superposition-and-generated-mixing).

Per-axis `pump_harmonics` and `modulation_harmonics` keep their separate
operating-point and small-signal meanings. Optional
`max_intermodulation_order=N` adds the finite-lattice crop

$$
\sum_j |m_j| \le N.
$$

Omitting it applies no additional diamond crop; the per-axis limits still make
the basis finite. A supplied `N` is a nonnegative integer and must retain every
declared drive and requested trace mode. `run.explain()` enumerates the actual
tuples, signed physical frequencies, source/trace bindings, and exact
tuple-frequency collisions. Exact collisions fail closed; SCNSim does not
invent a near-commensurability tolerance or Gate. See
[mixing order versus intermodulation truncation](https://github.com/arfiligol/SCQ_Design/blob/main/docs/knowledge/numerical-methods/harmonic-balance-periodic-steady-state.qmd#mixing-order-versus-intermodulation-truncation).

The operating-point lattice stores one signed ordinary frequency
$f_m=\sum_jm_jf_{p,j}$ per tuple. The linear-response lattice stores the full
ordered grid

$$
f_{k,m}=f_k+\sum_jm_jf_{p,j},\qquad \omega_{k,m}=2\pi f_{k,m},
$$

for every requested `spec.frequencies[k]` and every input/output tuple. Each
mode grid must match the request grid and the matrix leading dimension in
length and order. Zero-frequency preflight, $W_{\mathrm{in/out}}$, signed-mode
permutation, and reconciliation all consume these full grids; no single sample
or tuple-only offset may stand in for them.

`HBSolveSpec.allow_driven_ptc` defaults to `False`. If a selected Ref contains
PTC and any case has nonzero effective DC or AC operating-point drive, the
complete request fails preflight unless this override is explicit. Undriven
cases remain exact PTC realizations. An authorized driven case instead solves
the static/nonlinear balance on the original Plan with probe shunts present,
then applies PTC only to the response linearized around that loaded operating
point. Result and receipt must say `loaded balance` and `compensated analysis
topology`; they cannot claim an unloaded operating point.

HB numerical controls are runtime-owned and have no public override object or
keyword. V1 binds Julia `1.12.6`, JosephsonCircuits `0.5.4`, one Julia/BLAS
thread, `iterations=1000`, `ftol=1e-8`,
`switchofflinesearchtol=1e-5`, `alphamin=1e-4`, and `nbatches=1` in the HB
algorithm identity. Each case starts independently from `x0=zeros`, runs in
declaration order, and never inherits another case's operating point.

SCNSim does not treat an upstream maximum-iteration warning as success. After
the backend returns a candidate state `x`, it recomputes the final residual
`F` and accepts that case only when

$$
\lVert F\rVert_\infty \le 10^{-8}
\quad\text{or}\quad
\left(\lVert x\rVert_2>0\ \text{and}\
\frac{\lVert F\rVert_2}{\lVert x\rVert_2}<10^{-8}\right).
$$

Otherwise that declared case receives an `HBCaseFailure`. These fixed controls
and this check are product behavior, not a user-selectable convergence Gate.
`max_intermodulation_order` maps to both backend pump and modulation lattice
crops, and a request containing any `mode=()` drive enables DC terms for every
case so their common basis remains exact. The complete adapter and artifact
mechanics are fixed in
[HB Realization and Outcomes](implementation/hb-realization-and-outcomes.qmd).

### Required lineage and receipt evidence

The durable evidence chain for every terminal `AnalysisResult` binds the sealed
Plan, compiled operator, ParameterSet, ordered Ref lineage,
retained/eliminated coordinates, selected channel order, and exact runtime
identity. Those records remain owned by their canonical Plan, request, Result,
artifact, and receipt documents rather than being duplicated into every public
Result object.

The Plan/compile evidence records every exact Library and component-schema
identity, component hierarchy and public schema, pin-to-electric-node/ground
mapping, Public/Internal/Port-promoted node identities, canonical ground and
backend-node-zero mapping, explicit and built-in local ground groups, logical
Port mapping,
source units and canonical SI values, public ParameterRefs, expanded
primitive/backend rows, and Direct/HB realization. Composite evidence includes
public parameters/baselines, identity fan-out, AffineMap equations/support,
public pins/coordinates, and hidden-child expansion. RLGC evidence includes
conductor/reference identity, complete matrix order and health, positive
head-to-tail series-current/extractor `+z` orientation, manual/Q2D source
classification, parsed canonical values, extraction frequency, content-derived
provenance, transmission-line pi-ladder convention, section count, and bound
section length; all three IDC capacitance branches, each JJ
and optional parallel `Cj`, the two shared-parameter
SQUID junctions and finite loop, and every coupled branch orientation with
bound `L1`, `L2`, signed `k`, derived `M`, and backend mapping. The authoring
surface and its fail-closed rules are defined in
[V1 Component Authoring](component-authoring.qmd). The exact recursively sealed
graph and deterministic lowering are fixed in
[Composite Snapshots and Recursive Expansion](implementation/composite-snapshots-and-recursive-expansion.qmd),
while distributed-line parsing and expansion are fixed in
[RLGC, Q2D, and Pi Expansion](implementation/rlgc-q2d-and-pi-expansion.qmd).

In the `dev4` slice, `run.explain()` materializes expanded branch rows,
`omitted-as-zero` labels, and derived mutual-inductance mappings. Terminal
receipts bind the sealed Plan, request, and exact runtime identities; they do
not duplicate those compiler-row diagnostics as a second evidence schema.

A logical Port record includes its identity, role, reference impedance,
node/coordinate attachment, and one-Port-per-node evidence. Direct records
`B`, `Y0`, `G_port`, voltage/current and wave conversion, plus `P row = not
applicable`; HB records exact `P_i`/`R_port_i` rows, solver indices, mode order,
and raw-Z lineage.

A PTC lineage additionally records selected `PortRef` identities, proved load
stamps, original-Port load mask, load state before/after compensation, resolved
resistances, removal intent, raw-Z/derived-intrinsic-operator identities,
per-probe `raw`/`compensated` labels, and reconstruction or residual evidence.

Every `transform_pair()` lineage additionally records its exact ordered Public
node inputs, Port-realizability mapping and current directions, all included
external-cut branches, all
excluded direct-mutual branches, resolved weights, power-conjugate maps,
transformed real-SPD reference matrix, principal root and reconstruction
evidence, and generated coordinate order. These obligations apply whether or
not the lineage contains PTC.

Every `retain()` lineage records the ordered retained coordinates, complete
eliminated complement, final selected-view channel order, and exact
full-row-rank `A_k`, injection `B_k`, induced reference `R_k`, principal root
`D_k`, wave map `Q_k`, selected/omitted projectors, omitted matched loads,
selected source boundary, and public-network de-embedding evidence.
The canonical step order, recomputation boundary, and N-port realization are
fixed in
[View Lineage and Selected Networks](implementation/view-lineage-and-selected-networks.qmd).

Every HB Result additionally records the request-global pump-axis and drive
schemas; operating-point and modulation limits; optional intermodulation crop;
three-/four-wave-mixing selections; retained mode tuples, signed frequencies,
and mode-port order; solver normalization and version; input/output `W`
matrices; solver-to-SCNSim phasor, mode-index, and `returnZ`/`returnS`
conversion, same-signed-frequency permutation, and single-conjugation proof;
and the source-loaded, intrinsic, selected-network, and reconciliation
identities.
Each case records its declared current contributions, generated conjugates,
SCNSim-to-solver coefficient/index map, oriented injection maps, effective
mode-indexed source vectors, derived Bias/Pump states, and exact case identity.
A driven PTC Result also records
`allow_driven_ptc`, loaded balance topology, and compensated analysis topology.

Direct quantity and optimization receipts additionally record quantity-spec
identity, selector and dimensionality, root/pole/zero branch and its declared
locator, the `DiagonalRootSpec.root_hint`, baseline selection, continuation and
local slope/residue evidence where applicable, shared dependency nodes, expanded
residual scale and source, objective weight, candidate failure ledger, and the
one Julia-process execution identity. The canonical optimization request owns
model-default bounds, any immutable consumer overrides, resolved bounds, and
the authorization set. Its receipt retains those roles only transitively by
binding that request hash; receipt-local evidence records AffineMap
support/extrapolation outcomes and authorization provenance, physical candidate
values, dimensionless optimizer coordinates, and the source-unit spelling used
by the executed attempt. It never duplicates a second bounds authority.

### Direct and HB component realization

Both backends consume the same expanded Plan. R, L, and C rows stay linear.
Direct lowers complete validated RLGC matrices; HB lowers complete C/G and L
but requires diagonal R. A nonzero off-diagonal R fails HB preflight without
altering the Direct-capable Plan. Direct realizes each JJ with its declared zero-phase,
zero-bias `L_J0` and retains any explicit parallel `Cj`; it does not accept an
arbitrary bias phase in V1. HB retains the nonlinear Josephson rows. A symmetric
SQUID remains a two-junction finite-loop topology in both paths: Direct uses two
`L_J0` small-signal branches, while HB keeps both nonlinear junctions, the loop,
and any mutual pump coupling.

JosephsonCircuits is only the HB backend. Its official
[flux-pumped JPA example](https://josephsoncircuits.org/stable/#Flux-pumped-Josephson-parametric-amplifier-(JPA))
describes flux-pump and three-wave-mixing support as relatively untested;
SCNSim records that backend limitation instead of enlarging its guarantee.

RLGC acceptance is strict on the canonical Float64 matrices. Reciprocity uses
exact symmetry; Maxwell C/G signs and row sums must already have their required
signs; C/L must pass unpivoted symmetric Cholesky; and the minimum eigenvalue of
G/R must be nonnegative. SCNSim does not symmetrize, clip, project, add a
grounding correction, or retain a corrected matrix beside the raw source.
Failure names the exact matrix invariant rather than manufacturing a usable
line model.

### Operation support

| Selected Ref lineage | Direct evaluate/optimize | Direct solve | HB solve |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Original | Yes | all logical Ports | all logical Ports |
| PTC | Yes | Yes | Yes; driven PTC requires authorization |
| `transform_pair()` over a complete Port-bound node pair | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| `retain()` of only Port-realizable coordinates | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Named unported Public node or transform involving one | Yes | No | No |

Physical compilation belongs to the original Plan and is not presented as a
separate reduced compile action. Terminal operations materialize or exactly
resolve the required original and selected-view stages internally.

## Direct matrices and physical quantities

### Common matrix surface

Direct and HB expose the same selected-view S/Y/Z families without pretending
their enclosing Results are identical:

```python
direct.s.view
direct.y.view
direct.z.view

case = hb.cases["dc_pump_a_low"]
case.s.view
case.y.view
case.z.view
```

HB may additionally expose backend-native and reconciliation evidence. Direct
does not acquire a fake case layer. S display accepts
`magnitude="linear" | "db"`; dimensionful Y/Z matrices remain linear Quantity
surfaces.

For the canonical $e^{-i\omega t}$ convention, the Direct circuit admittance is

$$
Y_{\mathrm{circ}}(\omega)
=\frac{D(\omega)}{-i\omega}
=G-i\omega C+\frac{i}{\omega}K.
$$

`DirectSolveSpec.frequencies` is one SCNSim-registry frequency Quantity whose
magnitude is a non-empty, one-dimensional, finite, strictly increasing,
duplicate-free grid with every $f>0$. The first slice rejects scalar, ragged,
unordered, repeated, zero, and negative grids before starting an attempt.

At each grid point the angular frequency used in $D(\omega)$ and
$Y_{\mathrm{circ}}(\omega)$ is $\omega=2\pi f$ after coherent-SI conversion.

At every requested point SCNSim must form finite selected-network Y, Z, and S.
A failed Schur complement, source-boundary solve, Y-to-Z solve, or Y-to-S solve
fails the whole request as `DirectResponseFormationError` with the exact stage.
It publishes no partial grid, pseudoinverse, infinity, or stale family. For
every required $AX=B$, including multiple right-hand
sides, SCNSim computes the normalized backward residual

$$
\eta(A,X,B)=
\frac{\lVert AX-B\rVert_\infty}
{\lVert\lvert A\rvert\lvert X\rvert+\lvert B\rvert\rVert_\infty},
$$

where absolute values are entrywise complex magnitudes and the matrix infinity
norm is the maximum absolute row sum. Exact `0/0` is zero; a zero denominator
with nonzero numerator is infinity. All operands and the resulting residual
must be finite, and

$$
\eta(A,X,B)\le\tau(n),\qquad
\tau(n)=256(n+1)\,\epsilon_{\mathrm{Float64}}.
$$

Here $n$ is the order of the square $A$ being checked. An empty complement that
requires no solve is a no-op rather than a zero-dimensional factorization.
The residual is a mandatory execution-time Gate but its raw value is not a
public Result or receipt field. Condition number is neither a Gate nor a
required computation.
The exact-open one-Port identity $Y=0,\ S=+1$ remains an internal algebra probe;
because finite Z does not exist, it cannot become a successful complete public
`DirectSolveResult`.

### Typed Direct quantity catalog

`run.evaluate()` evaluates one declared Direct physical quantity or
materializes the full dynamic operator without requiring an unrelated response
sweep:

```python
readout_root = DiagonalRootSpec(
    coordinate="readout_node",
    root_hint=6.0 * u.GHz,
)

evaluated = run.evaluate(quantity_view, readout_root)

evaluated.root
evaluated.frequency
evaluated.linewidth
evaluated.slope
```

For a named retained coordinate $r$, this request solves the defining complex
root problem

$$
\left[\mathbf D_R^{E\downarrow}(\widetilde\Omega_r)\right]_{rr}=0.
$$

The selected Ref determines what this diagonal means. Retaining one authored
node eliminates its complement with `I_external = 0`; logical-Port loads and
other uncompensated stamps remain in the effective operator. The resulting
root is therefore loaded when those attachments are present. It is not the
uncoupled LC formula, a minimum or dip read from S, or a hybridized pole of a
larger retained block.

Required `root_hint` is a Quantity-valued approximate location used only to
start deterministic complex Newton for one locally simple, machine-resolved
root at the sealed baseline ParameterSet. It is not
the returned root, an optimization target, a constraint, or an implicit search
window. The evaluated frequency may differ from the hint. A non-baseline
ParameterSet, including every optimization candidate, uses deterministic
continuation owned by the identified baseline root; it never selects whichever
root is then closest to the original hint or to the preceding CMA-ES candidate.
Missing or dimensionally invalid hints and detected repeated or
non-continuable roots fail closed.

The Primitive Direct E2E realization supports one retained coordinate and
requires the complete compiled capacitance matrix to be positive definite for
`DiagonalRootSpec`. Singular-C descriptor/infinite-mode handling remains a
later quantity scope; real-grid Direct S/Y/Z does not inherit this restriction.
The exact scalar Schur residual, analytic derivative, 32-update complex-Newton
limit, machine-resolution certificate, and deterministic dyadic continuation
are fixed in
[Diagonal-Root Numerical Procedure](implementation/diagonal-root-numerical-procedure.qmd).
V1 does not enumerate the complete QEP spectrum to certify this root.
Its certificate is machine-resolution evidence, not a validated global root or
analytic-branch enclosure; possible undetected Newton-basin exchange remains a
known V1 limitation.

`readout_root.frequency` on the Spec is an immutable selector that can be
placed in an objective; `evaluated.frequency` is the resulting Quantity. Merely
accessing the selector does not execute or consult process memory.

The V1 catalog is intentionally small:

| Spec | Declared operation | Public result |
|---|---|---|
| `DiagonalRootSpec` | Complex root of one named diagonal of the selected Direct dynamic operator | root, frequency, linewidth, slope |
| `HybridizedPoleSpec` | Complex root of the determinant of the terminal View's complete ordered retained block (at least two coordinates) | pole/root bundle with branch evidence |
| `TransferZeroSpec` | Complex zero of one ordered S/Y/Z input/output projection whose transfer denominator is finite and nonsingular at the candidate | zero bundle with numerator/denominator evidence; never a sweep minimum or implicit pole-zero cancellation |
| `ResidueNormalizedCouplingSpec` | Coupling from two selected machine-resolved branches with local slope/residue evidence and one declared evaluation point | complex coupling and magnitude |
| `ResponseElementSpec` | One S/Y/Z element at a declared frequency and ordered input/output coordinates | complex scalar and applicable real/imaginary/magnitude selectors |
| `OperatorSpec` | Full Direct dynamic operator on a declared grid | coordinate- and unit-bearing matrix Result |

```python
transmission = ResponseElementSpec(
    family="S",
    input_coordinate="feedline_in",
    output_coordinate="feedline_out",
    frequency=6.2 * u.GHz,
)

transfer_zero = TransferZeroSpec(
    anchor=6.5 * u.GHz,
    family="Y",
    input_coordinate=feedline_out_node,
    output_coordinate=filter_open_tail,
)

operator = run.evaluate(
    quantity_view,
    OperatorSpec(frequencies=frequency_grid),
)
```

Root-like bundles expose only physically defined typed scalar selectors such as
`.frequency`, `.linewidth`, `.magnitude`, `.real`, and `.imag`. Their branch,
branch locator (including `DiagonalRootSpec.root_hint`), continuation,
local slope/residue evidence, units, ParameterSet, selected Ref boundary, and
operator identity remain attached. `DiagonalRootSpec` promises the documented
machine-resolved Newton procedure, not a globally unique spectral root. A
locally repeated/non-simple pole or zero, or a coupling input without its
required local slope/residue evidence, fails closed under that quantity's own
contract.
`HybridizedPoleSpec.coordinates` must equal the terminal View's retained
coordinate sequence exactly; it cannot introduce a hidden second retain
boundary. A real hybrid/zero anchor initializes a real angular frequency, while
a complex anchor preserves both declared components under the $2\pi$
conversion. An anchor is a Newton-basin initializer, never a nearest-root
instruction.

`frequencyAnchor` keeps that distinction in the exact request bytes. A plain
real Quantity encodes as `quantity_f64`; a Python complex Quantity, including
one whose imaginary component is exactly `0`, encodes as
`complex_quantity_f64` with independently canonical real and imaginary SI
bits. Both forms retain the declared source-unit provenance in the receipt.
There is no lossy real fallback, compatibility alias, or implicit removal of a
zero imaginary component.
`TransferZeroSpec` currently exposes only an ordered S/Y/Z projection; a
generic cofactor/minor object is not part of the V1 scaffold. The Spec also
requires its selected transfer denominator to
remain finite and nonsingular at the zero. A coincident numerator zero and pole
is rejected as an unresolved cancellation rather than published as a transfer
zero.
For the canonical `exp(-i * Omega * t)` convention, `.root` is the complex
angular-frequency Quantity, `.frequency` is `real(Omega) / (2 * pi)`, and the
positive passive linewidth is `-2 * imag(Omega) / (2 * pi)`. The Result records
the convention instead of inferring a sign from a plotted trace.

`QuantitySum(a, b, ...)` is the only V1 scalar composition and is legal only
inside a `CostObjective`; it is not a standalone `run.evaluate()` request.
Every term must have the same dimensionality. SCNSim exposes no general
expression tree or Python callable objective. A consumer may still request `OperatorSpec` and use
its labeled Quantity matrix for ordinary Python/NumPy calculation; a full
operator or matrix cannot itself become one scalar cost.

The fixed local numerical procedures, analytic derivatives, branch evidence,
principal-square-root convention, continuation, artifact units, and typed
failure mapping for this catalog are defined in
[Direct Poles, Zeros, Couplings, and Operators](implementation/direct-poles-zeros-and-operators.qmd).
That page implements this catalog; it does not add a second public selector or
global root-search promise.

The reusable definitions remain canonical in SCQ_Design:
[anchored diagonal roots and hybridized poles](https://github.com/arfiligol/SCQ_Design/blob/main/docs/knowledge/numerical-methods/schur-complement-kron-reduction.qmd#anchored-bare-diagonal-roots-and-hybridized-poles),
[poles, zeros, and residues](https://github.com/arfiligol/SCQ_Design/blob/main/docs/knowledge/network-modeling/poles-zeros-residues.qmd),
and the
[local residue-normalized coupling](https://github.com/arfiligol/SCQ_Design/blob/main/docs/knowledge/network-modeling/poles-zeros-residues.qmd#local-residue-normalized-open-coupling).
SCNSim documents only how those quantities are selected, evaluated, and
evidenced.

## Optimization and numerical scaling

### Quantity objectives and one Julia execution

V1 optimization evaluates Direct objectives only. It accepts one selected
`NetworkViewRef`, any number of optimization variables, and any number of
scalar quantity objectives:

```text
Component Library author
  ParameterSpec + baseline + fan-out/AffineMap calibration support

Circuit-model author
  reusable default OptimizationSpec + variables/bounds/objectives/optimizer

Notebook consumer
  inspect the default + provide a Design Target + optional immutable override
```

Runtime slices change which already-declared selectors are executable, not the
View model or optimizer. `1.0.0.dev3` evaluates
`DiagonalRootSpec.frequency` and `.linewidth` on a supported retained quantity
View. Its original one-Port/no-trace restriction belongs only to that slice's
`solve_direct` response surface. `1.0.0.dev5` reuses the same CMA replay,
ledger, cache, retry, and winner contract while enabling
`HybridizedPoleSpec.frequency`/`.linewidth`, `TransferZeroSpec.frequency`,
`ResidueNormalizedCouplingSpec.magnitude`, and
`ResponseElementSpec.magnitude`/`.real`/`.imag`. Before its owning slice, each
selector fails fast with `ScaffoldUnavailableError`; it is not excluded from
full V1. `QuantitySum` remains legal only inside a `CostObjective`.

`ParameterSpec` never owns optimization bounds. A circuit-model package may
instead expose one clearly named model default:

```python
def build_default_optimization_spec(target) -> OptimizationSpec:
    return OptimizationSpec(
        variables=(
            OptimizationVariable(
                parameter=model.shared_short_length,
                bounds=(0.6 * u.mm, 1.2 * u.mm),
            ),
            OptimizationVariable(
                parameter=model.idc_finger_length,
                bounds=(40.0 * u.um, 68.0 * u.um),
            ),
        ),
        objectives=build_objectives(target),
        optimizer=CMAESSpec(seed=17, max_evaluations=400),
    )
```

The consumer discovers the recipe without reading its source:

```python
default_spec = model.build_default_optimization_spec(target)

model.idc_finger_length.show()
default_spec.show()
default_spec.variable(model.idc_finger_length).bounds
run.explain(optimization_view, default_spec).show()
```

These surfaces answer different questions. `parameter.show()` reports the
sealed baseline, unit, fan-out, maps, and calibration support;
`default_spec.show()` reports active variables, default bounds, quantity
objectives, weights, expanded normalization, and optimizer;
`run.explain()` reports the fully bound request that would execute. None starts
a solver or writes the workspace.

```python
qubit_root = DiagonalRootSpec(
    coordinate="qubit.differential",
    root_hint=4.8 * u.GHz,
)

optimization_spec = OptimizationSpec(
    variables=(
        OptimizationVariable(
            parameter=resonator.parameter("capacitance"),
            bounds=(80.0 * u.fF, 120.0 * u.fF),
        ),
        OptimizationVariable(
            parameter=coupler.parameter("coupling_coefficient"),
            bounds=(
                0.01 * u.dimensionless,
                0.20 * u.dimensionless,
            ),
        ),
    ),
    objectives=(
        CostObjective(
            id="readout_frequency",
            quantity=readout_root.frequency,
            target=6.2 * u.GHz,
            weight=100.0 * u.dimensionless,
        ),
        CostObjective(
            id="combined_linewidth",
            quantity=QuantitySum(
                qubit_root.linewidth,
                readout_root.linewidth,
            ),
            target=2.0 * u.MHz,
            weight=10.0 * u.dimensionless,
        ),
    ),
    optimizer=CMAESSpec(seed=17, max_evaluations=200),
)

optimization = run.optimize(quantity_view, optimization_spec)
```

The best values remain an immutable `ParameterSet`. Reusing them is an
explicitly new request and never mutates the Plan baseline or the selected
Ref:

```python
winner_root = run.evaluate(
    quantity_view,
    readout_root,
    parameters=optimization.best.parameters,
)
winner_root.frequency
```

The model default is immutable. A consumer creates a `custom_spec` only when a
notebook must depart from it:

```python
custom_spec = default_spec.with_variable_overrides(
    bounds={
        model.idc_finger_length: (
            38.0 * u.um,
            76.0 * u.um,
        ),
    },
    allow_extrapolation=(model.idc_finger_length,),
)
```

Overrides use exact `ParameterRef` keys. `show()` distinguishes
`model_default`, `consumer_override`, and resolved bounds; the request owns all
three and its receipt binds them transitively through the request hash. There
is no global extrapolation switch or second hidden bound source.
Calling `with_variable_overrides()` never mutates its source: original
model-default bounds remain fixed, named overrides replace any prior override,
and unmentioned overrides are preserved. Its `allow_extrapolation=` argument
is the complete authorization set for the returned Spec rather than an
implicit union with the source. The full Spec, resolved bounds, and sorted
authorization identities enter request identity; only authoring-unit spelling
stays evidence-only.

Each `AffineMap.support` is a calibration-evidence interval. Values inside it
need no authorization. An out-of-support value fails by default; a request may
approve extrapolation only for named `ParameterRef` objects. An unapproved
optimization candidate becomes
`InvalidCandidatePhysicalParameter(stage="affine_support")` with tagged `Inf`
cost. Every out-of-support fan-out records exactly one evidence entry: a
rejected candidate uses authorization source `none`, while an approved
candidate uses `optimization_spec` (or `parameter_set` for an ordinary
solve/evaluate receipt). Each entry records the public parameter, exact
consumer, support, input value, lower/upper side, canonical distance beyond
support, and authorization source without
claiming that Q2D or another calibration validated the extrapolated region.
Distance uses the public input/support dimensionality and coherent-SI value
`support_lower - input_value` on the lower side or
`input_value - support_upper` on the upper side, and is strictly positive.
Binding order is fixed: resolve the public value, check every fan-out support,
validate authorization, apply each `AffineMap`, then validate mapped primitive
physical domains. Candidate ledgers own candidate extrapolation evidence;
ordinary solve/evaluate receipts own evidence authorized by their explicit
`ParameterSet`.
Authorization is request-local: passing an extrapolated winner to a later
solve/evaluate request requires a new explicit ParameterSet approval:

```python
approved_winner = ParameterSet(
    optimization.best.parameters.values,
    allow_extrapolation=(model.idc_finger_length,),
)

direct = run.solve(response_view, direct_spec, parameters=approved_winner)
```

The original winner values remain immutable; candidate and winner
`ParameterSet.allow_extrapolation` are empty. The new request records its own
authorization instead of inheriting the optimizer's approval.

The public `run.evaluate()` contract does not force candidate work back through
Python. One optimization request launches one Julia process. Parameter binding,
candidate compilation, Ref-lineage replay, quantity evaluation, shared
