factorization/root work, objective aggregation, and CMA-ES remain inside that
process. Python submits the sealed request and receives process-local progress
and the final receipt; V1 has no per-candidate IPC/callback or persistent Julia
daemon. Repeated quantity identities share dependency nodes within a candidate.

The Julia process may emit generation-level JSONL progress for internal
presentation and diagnostics. Progress records never enter Plan, request,
optimization, candidate, or Result identity and cannot become a scientific
Gate. V1 exposes no `progress` keyword, callback framework, per-candidate
observer, public JobRef, or persistent daemon.

`CMAESSpec` has the fixed public surface

```python
CMAESSpec(
    seed=0,
    max_evaluations=200,
    population_size=None,
    initial_sigma=0.25,
)
```

For $n$ active variables, `population_size=None` resolves to
$\lambda=4+\lfloor3\ln n\rfloor$. The sealed baseline must lie inside every
bound, maps to the initial unit-box mean $m_0$, is evaluated first, consumes one
evaluation, and remains winner-eligible. Baseline evaluation failure fails the
request. `initial_sigma` is a positive finite unit-coordinate scale. `seed`
accepts a signed 64-bit integer; an explicit population size is an integer of
at least two, and the evaluation budget must be large enough for the required
complete generation.

The runtime pins
[CMAEvolutionStrategy.jl 0.2.6](https://github.com/jbrea/CMAEvolutionStrategy.jl/tree/v0.2.6),
registry tree `6bf0985be2c5ea58305d2d04e336684f64fdc12a`. Its public
`minimize()` initializes

$$
C_0=\operatorname{diag}\!\left(\exp(10^{-4}i/n)\right),
\qquad i=0,\ldots,n-1,
$$

rather than exact identity. SCNSim maps physical parameters once to
$z\in[0,1]$, calls `minimize(objective, baseline_z, initial_sigma, ...)`,
supplies `lower=zeros(n)`, `upper=ones(n)`, and
lets the package apply its lin-quad unit-box transform. SCNSim does not clip,
mirror, or apply another physical box transform. The signed Int64 seed is
reinterpreted as UInt64 with the same bits.

The fixed request identities are
`algorithm_id="scnsim.direct_cmaes.cmaes_jl_0_2_6_state_replay.v2"` and
`box_transform_id="cmaes-jl-0.2.6-linquad-unit-box.v1"`. The call uses
`popsize=lambda`, `maxiter=g`, `maxfevals=nothing`,
`parallel_evaluation=true`, `multi_threading=false`, and `verbosity=0`, with
ftol, xtol, stagnation, target, time, and noise controls set to `nothing`. Its
internal callback captures evaluated-generation evidence and emits progress;
it does not change sampling or stopping, and ledger sealing waits for the
continuation boundary below. With
budget $B$, it runs exactly
$g=\lfloor(B-1)/\lambda\rfloor$ complete generations and requires $g\ge1$;
unused remainder is evidence. Candidate failures and cache hits still consume
their declared population ordinal. The winner is the lowest finite cost among
the baseline and completed candidates; an exact cost tie selects the earliest
evaluation ordinal in baseline, generation, then population-column order.
These execution controls bound reproducibility but do not decide whether the
result meets a Design Target.

Every population outcome records both the callback-visible raw CMA sample
column `optimizer_latent_coordinates_f64` and its transformed unit-box
`optimizer_coordinates_f64` beside the physical bindings. Both arrays have
length $n$ in request-variable order. Retry invokes the
same pinned `minimize()` from the original seed. The batch objective verifies
the transformed coordinates, generation, and population column before
returning stored costs; the package callback then verifies the raw sample bits
before the mean or covariance update. The raw check is mandatory because the
lin-quad transform is many-to-one. The first unsealed generation resumes
physical evaluation. SCNSim neither serializes nor restores the package's
private optimizer object; either replay mismatch is `EvidenceIntegrityError`.

A callback precedes the package update and therefore cannot by itself seal a
resumable generation. Each verified ledger also carries the canonical
`cmaes-jl-0.2.6-julia-1.12.6-continuation-state.v1` certificate over all
future-affecting mean, sigma/path, covariance/decomposition, stop, constraint,
and exact MersenneTwister fields. For $k<g$, ledger $k$ becomes verified only at
callback $k+1$ before its update, under boundary
`post_update_post_next_sample_pre_next_update`; the certificate also covers the
next raw and transformed `[n, lambda]` populations. Interruption before that
boundary falls back to ledger $k-1$. The final ledger is certified only after
`minimize()` returns under `terminal_post_update`, with `Stop.it=g` and
`reason=:maxiter`. For sealed generations retry compares transformed samples
before returning stored costs. For the first unsealed generation it caches the
transformed sample, evaluates normally, and compares package state, RNG, raw
sample, and cached transformed sample against the preceding certificate in the
callback before update or evidence publication. These hashes are
continuation-integrity evidence, not independently reconstructable state
artifacts, and are never restored as optimizer state.

For every successful candidate, the ledger stores each objective's evaluated
Quantity, signed normalized residual, and weighted component cost in request
objective order. The request-owned target, resolved scale/source, and weight
must reproduce each component and their total. A candidate-dependent invalid
primitive value is `InvalidCandidatePhysicalParameter`; eliminated-block,
local-slope, and Newton/continuation failures retain their corresponding typed
root errors and tagged positive-infinity penalty. If any of those occurs while
evaluating the mandatory baseline, the request fails instead of creating an
optimization Result. Invalid variables, bounds, objectives, selectors, or
controls fail preflight as `InvalidOptimizationSpec`; a compiler invariant,
runtime failure, or process protocol failure aborts the request rather than
becoming a candidate outcome.

Julia package precompilation may reduce load and first-execution latency but
does not promise every specialization is already compiled. SCNSim adds no
special precompile workload until representative measurement shows startup is
material to this one-process boundary. See Julia's official
[execution-latency and precompilation guidance](https://docs.julialang.org/en/v1/manual/performance-tips/#Execution-latency,-package-loading-and-package-precompiling-time).

For every candidate, SCNSim binds its ParameterSet to the original Plan,
compiles that candidate, replays the complete selected Ref lineage, and
evaluates all objectives. A nominal reduced matrix is never reused across
different candidates. A singular/non-finite/branch failure is recorded as a
typed non-evaluable candidate, contributes `Inf` to the optimizer, and does not
publish stale or fallback quantities. Other candidates continue.

Optimization resume requires identical Plan, Ref, variables, quantity specs,
objectives, expanded normalization, algorithm, controls, seed, runtime, and
completed-generation ledger. An interrupted generation is discarded and
replayed deterministically rather than published as complete evidence.

### Tutorial realization {#ipf-optimization-example}

The Contract does not duplicate a complete workflow. The micro-course teaches
[primitive optimization](../examples/tutorials/04_optimize_primitive.qmd),
[general RLGC](../examples/tutorials/09_model_n_trace_line.qmd), and
[Direct/HB comparison](../examples/tutorials/13_compare_direct_hb.qmd) as
separate native-API operations without becoming a second contract authority.

### Relative objective normalization

Every objective uses

$$
r_i = \frac{q_i-t_i}{s_i},
\qquad
J = \sum_i w_i |r_i|^2.
$$

Normalization occurs before weighting, so `weight` expresses relative
importance rather than target magnitude or physical unit:

- for a nonzero target, omitted `scale` expands to `abs(target)`;
- for an exact zero dimensionless target, omitted `scale` expands to
  `1 * u.dimensionless`;
- for an exact zero dimensionful target, omitted `scale` fails closed; and
- an explicit positive, finite, same-dimensionality `scale` overrides those
  defaults.

SCNSim never divides by the current candidate `abs(q_i)`: that denominator is
undefined at zero and destroys optimization direction for a zero target. A
`CostObjective.weight` is required, positive, finite, and dimensionless. It
multiplies the squared residual as written above; it is not itself squared.
Explain/request/receipt surfaces store the expanded scale plus its source:
`relative_target`, `dimensionless_unity`, or `explicit`. These scales
nondimensionalize cost; they do not create a Gate, tolerance, or acceptance
rule. See the canonical
[normalized weighted objective](https://github.com/arfiligol/SCQ_Design/blob/main/docs/knowledge/numerical-methods/auditable-scientific-optimization.qmd#normalized-weighted-objective).

### Four distinct scaling contracts

SCNSim keeps these operations separate:

| Operation | Purpose | May change |
|---|---|---|
| Unit canonicalization | Give a physical value one SI identity | Representation only |
| Optimizer coordinate scaling | Prevent raw unit magnitude from controlling search coordinates | Optimizer coordinates only |
| Objective residual normalization | Make declared metric errors comparable | Only Human/Design-Target-declared objective terms |
| Linear-algebra conditioning | Improve numerical solution of the same operator | Internal representation only; never physics |

Every active `ParameterRef` appears exactly once. Its lower and upper bounds are
finite, have the parameter's dimensionality, satisfy $x_{i,\min}<x_{i,\max}$,
and contain the sealed baseline in the closed interval. Linear variables are
converted to one coherent SI unit and mapped to dimensionless unit-interval
coordinates:

$$
z_i = \frac{x_i-x_{i,\min}}{x_{i,\max}-x_{i,\min}} \in [0,1].
$$

The default is this linear map. When a variable explicitly declares
`transform="log"`, its lower bound, upper bound, and baseline must all be
strictly positive. Using their positive coherent-SI magnitudes $\widehat x$,
SCNSim instead uses the dimensionless ratio map

$$
z_i=
\frac{\ln(\widehat x_i/\widehat x_{i,\min})}
{\ln(\widehat x_{i,\max}/\widehat x_{i,\min})},
\qquad
\widehat x_i=
\widehat x_{i,\min}
\left(\frac{\widehat x_{i,\max}}{\widehat x_{i,\min}}\right)^{z_i}.
$$

Taking a logarithm of a dimensionful Quantity directly is never permitted.
Invalid order, dimensionality, positivity, duplicate variables, or an
out-of-bounds baseline fails before an attempt. The ledger records both
dimensionless optimizer coordinates and physical Quantity values.

Objective targets and weights remain consumer/Human declarations. The product
rule above deterministically expands an omitted residual scale; unit conversion
cannot alter that scale, the target, the weight, a tolerance, or a Gate.

### Linear algebra is not unit display

The small magnitude of an fF or nH value does not by itself prove that an
operator is ill-conditioned. Multiplying an entire equation by a scalar also
does not change its condition number.

SCNSim therefore does not expose a `ScalingSpec`, ScalingOptimizer, mutable
scale state, or automatic coordinate equilibration in Full V1.
Direct and Schur implementations must:

- use factorization/linear solves rather than an explicit inverse;
- compute and enforce every operation-specific normalized residual and
  machine-resolution certificate before publishing success; and
- keep those execution checks distinct from a Human-selected design-quality
  threshold.

Raw residuals, condition estimates, and complete numerical certificates are
not durable Result or receipt fields. A verified success states that the exact
operation algorithm ID and semantic runtime source digest completed every
required internal Gate. The Result stores the materialized answer and identity;
the receipt stores provenance and the hash chain. `resolve()` validates that
durable chain without recomputing the numerical checks. Re-evaluating the
numerical decision requires executing the same request again rather than
inferring it from omitted diagnostics.

If later public fixtures demonstrate a real raw-SI conditioning problem, the
shared solve boundary may add a deterministic, reversible equilibration. Its
map and inverse must be recorded, and it must preserve the physical operator,
observables, and Notebook API. Such evidence would reopen only that numerical
implementation scope.

## Results, display, and reports

`Result` means an immutable, already-materialized value whose inspection cannot
execute work. `AnalysisResult(Result)` is the receipt-backed terminal subset
returned by `solve()`, `evaluate()`, and `optimize()`. Every Analysis Result
exposes an immutable `ResultIdentity` containing its Plan, request, attempt, and
Result SHA-256 values. `DiagonalRootResult` is the concrete result of
`DiagonalRootSpec`; `resolve()` overloads preserve the corresponding concrete
type.

`ExplanationResult`, `CircuitDiagramResult`, and `ReportResult` are derived
Results. They do not fabricate request or receipt identity. `ReportSpec.inputs`
accepts explicit `AnalysisResult` objects, including inputs from different
Plans, and preserves each source identity independently.

### Typed Quantity results

Result scalar and array physical values use the SCNSim Pint registry. Consumers
can convert presentation units without changing result identity:

```python
frequencies = direct.frequencies.to(u.GHz)
matrix_si = operator.at(6.2 * u.GHz).matrix.to_base_units()
matrix_values = matrix_si.magnitude
root_frequency = evaluated.frequency.to(u.GHz)
probe_loads = direct.y.view.probe_loads
```

Each `AnalysisResult` carries its exact Result/Ref identity for serialization
and audit; derived Results preserve their explicit source identities instead of
inventing an operation receipt. Every matrix view also carries the ordered
coordinate IDs, exact flattened input/output `(coordinate, mode)` channel
labels, and its per-probe `raw`/`compensated` load-state mapping. Direct uses
the empty mode tuple; HB uses coordinate-major/mode-minor channel order.
Passing typed Results is the normal downstream UX; raw receipt paths remain an
audit surface.

### Display is explicit

`result.show()` returns the actual Figure, Drawing, or HTML presentation object.
Notebook and interactive frontends may display that object. Headless use simply
returns it and never claims that a window opened. Presentation cannot execute,
interpolate, or alter result identity.

`plot()` is not a universal Result method. Only a Result subtype with a natural
figure contract exposes it. Plot methods return the supported figure object so
the caller can display, save, or further configure it.

### HB case outcomes, traces, and display {#hb-cases-traces-and-display}

A completed HB request returns an `HBBatchResult`. Its public case index is one
ordered, read-only mapping keyed by every unique ID declared in `HBSolveSpec`.
Each value is an `HBCaseOutcome`, including a case that failed numerically:

```python
unbiased = hb.cases["unbiased"]
dc_only = hb.cases["dc_only"]
dc_pump_a_low = hb.cases["dc_pump_a_low"]
dc_two_tone = hb.cases["dc_two_tone"]

assert unbiased.succeeded
assert unbiased.bias_state is BiasState.OFF
assert unbiased.pump_state is PumpState.OFF
assert dc_only.bias_state is BiasState.ON
assert dc_only.pump_state is PumpState.OFF
assert dc_pump_a_low.bias_state is BiasState.ON
assert dc_pump_a_low.pump_state is PumpState.ON
assert dc_two_tone.pump_state is PumpState.ON
```

`hb.topology_evidence` is the immutable request-global record of the loaded
nonlinear balance and raw or PTC-compensated response lineage. Each successful
case separately exposes `operating_point_closure`, including the exact
absolute/relative residual evidence and successful disjunct (or the closed
no-operating-lattice not-applicable reason). A failed case has no success-only
closure record; its failure identity instead binds stage, message, ordinal,
case ID, and the complete effective-source evidence.

`HBBatchResult` does not implement `hb[id]`. `PumpState` is a derived
classification on each successful outcome, not an alternate lookup key. `BiasState`
independently records effective all-zero-mode drive. A case whose declared
drives sum to zero remains addressable by its declared ID while reporting the
corresponding Off states.

A successful outcome exposes S/Y/Z, traces, normalized node-flux `states`,
`BiasState`, and `PumpState`
directly, and its `failure` property is `None`. A failed outcome exposes
`succeeded=False` and `failure: HBCaseFailure`, whose stable `kind`, `stage`,
`message`, and evidence identity are receipt-backed. It also preserves case
identity and effective sources. Accessing S/Y/Z, traces, or success-only states
on that failed outcome raises that same `HBCaseFailure`; it never returns
`None`, an empty matrix, or a stale value.

`states` is operating-point evidence, not a `NetworkViewRef`, coordinate
handle, or drive target. It cannot be supplied to `retain()`,
`transform_pair()`, or `CurrentDrive.at`; anonymous Internal nodes remain
non-selectable. Its ordered state-node map matches the compiler node order and
the array's node axis exactly: Plan Public/port-promoted nodes map back to the
sealed Plan, Composite-private nodes map by component-path segments plus their
private-node ID, and anonymous Internal nodes expose only their
`internal-<sha256>` audit identity. The adapter derives the weber-valued
$\Phi^-_{m,n}=\varphi_0\operatorname{conj}(x^+_{\mathrm{JC},m,n})$ artifact
from the fixed backend state while `returnnodeflux=false`; it does not request
or publish a second backend node-flux authority.

A valid request may therefore produce a fully successful, partially
successful, or all-numerical-failure batch. All three are completed, verified
`HBBatchResult` receipts and are reused by the same request; a case numerical
failure does not make the request retryable. A process, protocol,
runtime-preparation, or receipt-integrity failure remains a request-level
failure rather than a fabricated case outcome, so a later identical operation
may append a new attempt.

An `SParameterTrace` names one complex matrix projection across the request's
frequency grid. Its `input_port` and `output_port` fields are selected-view wave
channel IDs, not necessarily original logical Port IDs. A channel generated by
`transform_pair()` is valid when the terminal view is Port-realizable. Mode
tuples must match the number and ordering of the HB pump axes. Trace IDs are
unique within the spec. A Direct spec may use the same trace type with empty
mode tuples.

Named traces are typed projections of the complete selected-view matrix. They
do not launch separate solves, hide the full matrix, or become another
physical authority:

```python
case = hb.cases["dc_pump_a_low"]

case.traces["signal_gain"].show()
case.s.view
case.y.view
case.z.view
case.s.backend_native
case.s.reconciliation
case.s.show()
```

`case.s.view` is the SCNSim selected-view generalized power-wave matrix.
`case.s.backend_native` preserves the backend-returned matrix, basis, reference,
and normalization. `case.s.reconciliation` records the exact conversion and
residual evidence when topology, load, boundary, reference plane, reference
matrix, frequency, and normalization are comparable.

Canonical selected HB matrix storage is the flattened three-dimensional stack
`[F, N_out * M_out, N_in * M_in]`. Each channel label is an exact
`(coordinate, mode)` pair in coordinate-major/mode-minor order; there is no
implicit five-dimensional reshape. Native evidence uses original logical-Port
major/mode-minor labels. Lift the Port-space map rather than applying it
directly to the mode-by-Port matrix:

$$
\mathcal Q_{k,\mathrm{in}}=Q_k\otimes I_{M_{\mathrm{in}}},
\qquad
\mathcal Q_{k,\mathrm{out}}=Q_k\otimes I_{M_{\mathrm{out}}}.
$$

For equal topology, reference plane, signed-frequency order, normalization,
and load mask, the comparable evidence is

$$
S_k=\mathcal Q_{k,\mathrm{out}}
S_{\mathrm{native,pw}}
\mathcal Q_{k,\mathrm{in}}^T.
$$

Comparable evidence preserves the unreplicated physical $Q_k$ in deterministic
row-major form and binds it to its Plan/View producer identity. Receipt loading
reconstructs the lifted projection and independently reproduces the selected S
matrix and recorded residual; a self-consistent but forged residual string is
not accepted.

A plain subset of original Ports is therefore comparable by its principal
submatrix when every omitted Port retains its native matched load. A PTC or
other unequal boundary is not comparable merely because channel names match.
In that case the reconciliation surface reports `comparable=False`, one exact
reason discriminator (`topology`, `load_or_ptc`, `reference_plane`,
`reference_matrix`, `signed_frequency_grid`, `channel_basis`, or
`normalization`), and the SHA-256 identity of the longest canonical Ref-lineage
prefix that remained comparable; it is neither `None` nor a fabricated
residual.

Batch display supports both declared traces and complete-matrix inspection:

```python
hb.show(theme=Theme.AUTO)  # magnitude="linear"
hb.show(magnitude="db", theme=Theme.DARK)
hb.cases["dc_pump_a_low"].show(theme=Theme.LIGHT)
hb.cases["dc_pump_a_low"].s.show(magnitude="db", theme=Theme.AUTO)
```

When traces are declared, `hb.show()` creates one panel per trace and overlays
the cases in declaration order. With no named traces, it expands every element
of each requested selected-view response matrix and overlays the same cases.
An overlay requires identical selected-view port, mode tuple, signed-frequency,
reference-plane, reference-matrix, and wave-normalization identities across
the cases. The request-global pump axes normally establish those identities;
any backend mismatch fails the presentation with the exact mismatched identity
rather than drawing incomparable lines. The full-matrix fallback applies the
same rule. It does not guess S21, truncate the matrix, rerun a request,
interpolate, or mix backend-native evidence into the selected-view plot.

For a partially successful batch, `hb.show()` plots only the successful
outcomes and appends a visible failed-case summary containing every failed case
ID and typed reason. It never silently omits a declared case. An all-failed
numerical batch produces the failure summary without inventing an empty plot or
promoting any case to success.

Complex S display shows magnitude and wrapped phase in `[-180 deg, 180 deg]`.
The default `magnitude="linear"` displays `abs(S)`. `magnitude="db"` displays
`20 log10(abs(S))`; an exact zero remains `-inf dB` without an epsilon, floor,
or clipping, and its phase is shown as undefined rather than zero. This option
changes presentation only. Dimensionful Y/Z results retain their
Quantity-valued linear presentation.

### Independent Direct and HB grids {#independent-direct-and-hb-grids}

Direct and HB Results retain the exact grids requested by their own Specs.
SCNSim does not create a hidden shared grid, interpolate one Result onto the
other, or derive pointwise residuals merely because both Results describe the
same selected network.

`show()` and Report presentation may overlay traces that use different grids;
each curve keeps its own coordinates and identity. Numerical comparison is an
explicit downstream calculation on already materialized typed scalar
Quantities with compatible dimensionality. V1 adds no general `compare()` API
and does not infer peaks, dips, bandwidths, roots, or resonances from plotted
curves.

### Explicit downstream sources

Reports name every source rather than selecting a latest result:

```python
direct_report = run.build_report(
    ReportSpec(inputs=(direct, evaluated), theme=Theme.AUTO)
)

report = run.build_report(
    ReportSpec(inputs=(direct, hb), theme=Theme.DARK)
)
```

Report assembly records the exact chosen inputs and may combine a Direct
response with a typed quantity, include one complete HB batch and its declared
successful/failed case outcomes, or present one exact optimization result and
its candidate/failure evidence. An individual HB case is derived within its
batch and is not a separate `AnalysisResult`; using the batch preserves the one
terminal receipt. Report assembly never changes which candidate is best or
turns a Design Target into a pass/fail Gate.

`ReportResult.save(path)` accepts only a new `.html` path whose parent already
exists. It refuses overwrite, writes atomically, and returns a `Path`. The
single self-contained HTML embeds plots, summary tables, and every
source identity, but not complete large raw arrays, workspace links,
timestamps, or inferred PASS/FAIL claims.

`ReportSpec.theme` accepts only `Theme.AUTO`, `Theme.LIGHT`, or `Theme.DARK`.
The report body, tables, and embedded Direct/HB SVG share that one theme.
`AUTO` uses self-contained `prefers-color-scheme` rules with a readable light
fallback; explicit themes stay fixed regardless of host UI.

An invalid suffix raises `ValueError`, a missing parent raises
`FileNotFoundError`, and an existing target raises `FileExistsError`; other
filesystem failures remain their ordinary `OSError` subtype. Report export is
derived presentation and never creates an analysis attempt or receipt.

## Authoring and compiled schematics

Schematics belong to the physical authority, so both representations start at
the Plan rather than a reduced Ref:

```python
diagram = plan.render_schematic()
diagram.show()
```

Omitting the Spec selects the human-readable `authoring` representation,
automatic light/dark theme selection, and IDs without parameter values. The
explicit surface is:

```python
from scnsim import CircuitDiagramSpec, Theme

diagram = plan.render_schematic(
    CircuitDiagramSpec(
        representation="authoring",  # or "compiled"
        theme=Theme.AUTO,             # or Theme.LIGHT / Theme.DARK
        show_parameter_values=True,
    )
)
diagram.show()
```

Raw strings and all other non-`Theme` values raise `TypeError` before a
diagram, numerical figure, or report is rendered. In Notebook rich display,
`Theme.AUTO` supplies self-contained SVG/HTML with a light fallback and a
`prefers-color-scheme: dark` override that changes foreground and background
together. `Theme.LIGHT` and `Theme.DARK` are fixed and self-contained. Direct
`Drawing.save()` and `Figure.savefig()` preserve explicit themes, while
`Theme.AUTO` always writes the portable light fallback. Theme choice never
enters Plan, request, Result, receipt, artifact, or workspace identity.

The `authoring` representation draws the semantic components, Public nodes,
logical Ports, canonical ground, anonymous junctions, and declared connections.
Grounded LC components expand visually into their parallel L/C branches with a
shared local bottom bus and one ground glyph rather than an opaque box. One
`ground(*pins)` call defines the same local bus/glyph group for ordinary
primitives; separate calls draw separate glyphs while remaining one electrical
ground. The renderer never replaces them with a page-wide ground bus. Larger
composites retain recognizable authoring symbols instead of compiler ladders.
Every visible object traces to the Plan.

Generic two-terminal symbols place `terminal_1` left and `terminal_2` right,
or top and bottom for a downward grounded branch. Rotation moves anchors but
never renames pins or reverses their physical orientation. A custom N-terminal
black box without a dedicated symbol places its ordered Library pin schema
clockwise from the lower-left boundary; this is renderer fallback only, not
compiler or pin-identity authority.

The `compiled` representation runs only the deterministic structural compile
preflight needed to materialize the complete baseline physical graph. It is
the audit view for primitive expansions, including every transmission-line pi
section. It is not a Direct or HB lowering and contains no backend rows, PTC,
coordinate transform, Schur reduction, or selected-view equivalent. Those
facts remain available through `run.explain(ref, spec).show()`.

`render_schematic()` requires a structurally complete valid Plan but does not
seal or mutate it, solve an analysis, or write a workspace. A compiled diagram
records the Plan, compiler, and expanded-graph identities. Values, when
requested, are baseline values: scalars appear near components, while complete
matrix or multi-field values appear in an ID-keyed legend or table without
truncation or unreadable layout compression.

`CircuitDiagramResult.show()` only presents the materialized diagram. It never
recompiles or executes. Diagram identity is separate from Plan and numerical
receipt identity; a theme/layout change or rendering failure cannot change or
block numerical analysis. SCNSim exposes neither `plan.show()` nor schematic
`.plot()`, and reduced Refs are inspected as operations and evidence rather
than fabricated equivalent circuits.

The compiled view maps every explicit ground group, grounded built-in return,
and pi-section station-local C/G shunt bus to Plan ground and JosephsonCircuits
node `"0"`. Simulation identity canonicalizes the union of grounded endpoints;
diagram identity additionally preserves the endpoint-derived local grouping.

## Failure and evidence contract

SCNSim-specific failures derive from `SCNSimError` through exactly five categories:
`SCNSimValidationError`, `SCNSimStateError`, `SCNSimCapabilityError`,
`SCNSimExecutionError`, and `SCNSimEvidenceError`. Every typed failure exposes
a stable machine `kind`, an exact `stage`, and immutable evidence. A started
operation seals its typed failure receipt before raising; preflight validation
creates no attempt. `resolve()` reconstructs the typed failure boundary but,
without a verified success, raises `ResultUnavailableError` and never retries.
Runtime preparation precedes request/attempt mutation; its failure raises
`RuntimePreparationError` without an attempt and leaves any already Plan-bound
Run workspace intact. Once an attempt is allocated, child launch failure and
every later missing or invalid outcome are attempt-backed
`BackendProtocolError` failures with a sealed failure receipt. Allocation
reserves ordinal/staging only; a blocked bootstrap lets Python finalize one
truthful immutable `allocated` or `launched` attempt record before numerical
execution begins.

The current public scaffold machine-maps `PlanSealedError`,
`WorkspacePlanReplacedError`,
`WorkspaceVersioningDowngradeForbidden`,
`UnsupportedRuntimePlatformError`, `PortRealizabilityError`,
`InvalidDiagonalRootHint`, `InvalidOptimizationSpec`,
`DirectResponseFormationError`, `InvalidCandidatePhysicalParameter`,
`CompilerInvariantError`,
`UnsupportedSingularCapacitanceForDiagonalRootV1`,
`EliminatedBlockSolveFailure`, `RootSlopeUnresolved`,
`NumericalResolutionUnresolved`, `HBCaseFailure`, `RuntimePreparationError`,
`BackendProtocolError`, `ResultUnavailableError`, `EvidenceIntegrityError`, and
`ScaffoldUnavailableError`. The last is reserved for explicitly deferred
surfaces; it cannot represent an attempted numerical failure.

Ordinary Python call-signature and filesystem errors retain their standard
exception types where the Contract says so; they are not backend failure
receipts disguised as SCNSim numerical errors.

SCNSim fails closed for:

- an attempted `versioned=True` to `versioned=False` workspace downgrade, a
  malformed versioned index, duplicate Plan-to-iteration mapping, or replaced
  workspace accessed through a stale Run/Result handle;
- a request directory whose canonical request differs from the sealed Plan,
  Ref, Spec, ParameterSet, runtime, or operation; a second writer for the same
  workspace; or an attempt that would overwrite prior evidence;
- a duplicate component, Public node, logical Port, or coupling identity, a
  reserved `"ground"` node collision, or duplicate pin/public-parameter names
  inside one component schema;
- an unknown pin, parameter, inductive branch, node, or unbound/foreign Library
  instance; a pin assigned to different nodes or ground groups; an empty
  `ground()` call; a foreign, duplicate, or already-assigned grounded pin; or
  an invalid/foreign/duplicate `ElectricNodeRef` or `PortRef`;
- an empty electric-node declaration or the same pin repeated within one node;
- an anonymous node promotion that collides with another Public identity; an
  anonymous unported node with fewer than two distinct pins; a second Port on
  one node; a Port bound to ground or directly to a pin; or a Port that
  changes its promoted node identity after seal;
- a non-positive physical leaf R/L/C/`L_J0`, negative `Cj`, invalid RLGC
  conductor/reference identity, matrix shape/order/units, inexact symmetry,
  invalid Maxwell sign/row sum, failed C/L Cholesky, negative G/R minimum
  eigenvalue, invalid AEDT Q2D primary blocks or conductor map, or
  non-positive/non-integer section count;
- a Direct/HB general-line mismatch, including nonzero off-diagonal R in HB;
- an invalid Composite public/hidden identity, wired `CoordinateRef`, invalid
  `AffineMap` units/support/baseline, or mapped nonphysical child value;
- a SQUID without shared junction parameters or a valid finite loop;
- mutual coupling across Plans, across non-inductive or unoriented branches,
  or with non-finite/dimensionful `k`, `abs(k) >= 1`, or a complete bound
  inductance matrix that is not reciprocal positive definite;
- an unsupported component expansion or missing Direct/HB realization;
- an incomplete/invalid Plan requested for schematic rendering, an invalid
  diagram representation/theme, or an unauditable compiled expansion;
- a bare physical number, unknown unit, foreign registry, or dimensionality
  mismatch;
- a ParameterSet containing unknown refs, non-finite values, or another Plan
  family;
- invalid Port roles, reference impedance, load mapping, or ambiguous physical
  coordinates;
- an unknown, duplicate, terminated, foreign, or unevidenced PTC `PortRef`;
- repeated PTC or PTC ordered after `transform_pair()` or `retain()`;
- an automatic pair transform with unknown, duplicate, Internal, identically
  selected, differently referenced, or inconsistently oriented Public nodes;
- incomplete or ambiguous capacitor-branch provenance, a non-finite or
  negative physical branch capacitance, a non-positive external-cut sum, or a
  nonreciprocal compiled capacitance operator outside the declared scope;
- a non-finite or singular pair transform, a non-real/non-symmetric/non-SPD
  physical or transformed reference matrix, or failed principal-root
  reconstruction;
- a generated-coordinate collision, rank-deficient retained Port map, or
  inconsistent derived `A_k`, `B_k`, `R_k`, principal `D_k`, `Q_k`, or
  selected/omitted projector evidence;
- a `transform_pair()` across Port-bound nodes with different PTC/load states;
- an unknown or duplicate pump axis, drive, case, or trace identity; a drive
  bound outside the request; a non-positive/non-finite axis frequency; or an
  incomplete request-global drive materialization;
- a non-integer drive/trace mode, tuple-rank/order mismatch, non-current or
  non-finite drive Quantity, complex DC coefficient, or unknown drive/trace
  coordinate;
- an independently declared negative-mode partner, inconsistent current
  orientation/injection map, or invalid Fourier-coefficient materialization;
- an invalid per-axis harmonic declaration, negative/non-integer
  `max_intermodulation_order`, retained-lattice exclusion of a declared
  drive/requested trace mode, or exact tuple-frequency collision;
- any zero-frequency HB linear-response input or output mode;
- an empty, duplicate, unknown, or Internal retained-coordinate selector;
- a Direct or HB `solve()` view with a non-Port-realizable final coordinate;
- an HB pair transform involving any non-Port-bound input node;
- a PTC Ref paired with any nonzero effective DC or AC drive without explicit
  `allow_driven_ptc=True`;
- a non-full-rank transform or singular/non-finite Schur partition;
- disagreement between Direct and HB Port node, reference impedance, load, or
  selected-channel mappings;
- a duplicate optimization variable/objective ID, foreign or hidden
  `ParameterRef`, invalid physical bounds/coordinate transform, or foreign
  quantity selector;
- conflicting model-default/consumer-override bounds, an unknown override key,
  an out-of-support bound/candidate without per-ParameterRef extrapolation
  authorization, or extrapolation authorization inherited by another request;
- a bundle, full matrix/operator, or dimensionally invalid composition used as
  one scalar objective;
- a target/selector dimensionality mismatch, non-positive/non-finite weight or
  explicit scale, or a zero dimensionful target without explicit scale;
- a missing, non-finite, non-positive, or dimensionally invalid
  `DiagonalRootSpec.root_hint` (`InvalidDiagonalRootHint`);
- a sealed `CircuitPlan` authoring mutation;
- `DiagonalRootSpec` applied to a non-positive-definite complete capacitance
  matrix in the Primitive Direct V1
  (`UnsupportedSingularCapacitanceForDiagonalRootV1`), an unsolved eliminated
  block (`EliminatedBlockSolveFailure`), an unresolved/non-simple slope
  (`RootSlopeUnresolved`), or a complex-Newton machine certificate that does not
  close within 32 updates (`NumericalResolutionUnresolved`);
- deterministic diagonal-root continuation whose physical path, branch, or
  subdivision cannot be completed, reported with its typed non-continuable
  failure rather than a different root;
- a locally repeated/non-simple pole or zero, or a residue-coupling input
  without the local slope/residue evidence required by its quantity spec;
- a transfer-zero candidate with a non-finite or singular denominator, or an
  unresolved pole-zero cancellation;
- a missing or mismatched exact receipt during resolve;
- an HB backend result that cannot bind complete mode-port Z, signed
  frequencies, input/output `W` normalization, phasor/mode-index conversion,
  or the required lifted operator identity;
- an HB adapter that reverses tuples and conjugates twice, cannot prove its
  same-signed-frequency permutation, or cannot de-embed every backend source
  resistor before selected-network construction;
- a missing or inconsistent per-case SCNSim-to-JosephsonCircuits source
  coefficient/conjugate-mode map;
- a returned HB case whose independently recomputed final residual satisfies
  neither fixed V1 condition, recorded as that case's `HBCaseFailure` rather
  than request success data;
- a selected matrix whose per-probe raw/compensated load-state labels do not
  match its lineage and stamps;
- an attempted reconciliation across unequal topology, PTC/load state,
  boundary, reference plane, reference matrix, frequency, or wave
  normalization;
- an optimization resume fingerprint, expanded-normalization identity, or
  completed-generation mismatch; or
- a corrupt request, receipt, or artifact hash.

V1 exposes no public timeout, JobRef, or cancellation object. A
`KeyboardInterrupt` terminates the active Julia child process, seals the
attempt as interrupted when its staging evidence is valid, and re-raises the
interrupt in Python. A later call to the same operation appends a new attempt;
`resolve()` does not continue or retry it.

Condition number is neither computed nor published by the V1 Direct/root
runtime. SCNSim does not invent conditioning thresholds, optimization Gates, search
envelopes, targets, weights, or acceptance conditions from backend defaults or
tests.

Diagram failure and an individual `HBCaseFailure` stay on their own evidence
surfaces. They cannot silently become successful numerical evidence or
overwrite unrelated success receipts.

## Known V1 limits

- Component authoring is limited to the explicit built-in catalog and custom
  Library contract in [V1 Component Authoring](component-authoring.qmd); there
  is no string discovery, mutable global registry, generic resonator topology
  enum, or arbitrary composite-child injection.
- Q2D ingestion accepts one primary general N-conductor R/L/G/C extraction and
  freezes its coefficients across the circuit solve grid. Frequency-dependent
  interpolation/extrapolation is not included, and HB rejects nonzero
  off-diagonal series R.
- Composite mapping is limited to identity fan-out and `AffineMap`; arbitrary
  callbacks, expression ASTs, and calibration-table interpolation are not
  included.
- Primitive Direct `DiagonalRootSpec` supports one retained coordinate with a
  positive-definite complete capacitance matrix. Singular-C descriptor roots
  and complete-QEP spectrum enumeration are not included. Deterministic dyadic
  continuation does not provide a validated global analytic-branch enclosure.
- Direct JJ/SQUID behavior is the declared zero-phase, zero-bias `L_J0`
  small-signal realization; arbitrary bias-point linearization is not included.
- JosephsonCircuits flux-pump and three-wave-mixing behavior retains its
  upstream relatively-untested limitation.
- HB V1 uses one fixed, versioned numerical policy and independent zero-state
  initialization per case. It exposes no `HBNumericsSpec`, warm-start policy,
  multithreaded batch mode, or callback hook.
- HB reduction acts on the small-signal sideband operator after the original
  nonlinear balance; nonlinear model-order reduction is not included.
- Driven PTC is a compensated small-signal view around a static/nonlinear
  balance that still contains the selected shunts; it is not an unloaded
  operating-point solution.
- Automatic `transform_pair()` is limited to the declared reciprocal lumped
  two-node capacitance scope. It is not universal modal diagonalization and
  V1 provides no manual-weight override through this API.
- HB optimization objectives are not included; optimization is Direct-only.
- Direct optimization accepts one selected Ref per request and no Python
  callable, general expression AST, or persistent Julia daemon.
- Quantization is not included.
- Direct and HB may use independent grids; comparison performs no implicit
  interpolation.
- No compatibility alias exists for the legacy Workbench import or bare-float
  physical inputs.
- No implicit latest-result selector exists.
- V1 has no public timeout, JobRef, cancellation API, callback progress
  framework, or persistent Julia daemon.
- Schematic auto-layout is deterministic Grid + Attach, not a general
  constraint solver.
- V1 has no public linear-algebra scaling configuration.
